docs.title: Smallcap stocks rally up to 21% in 2 days: Should you chase the rush or book profits?
docs.text:
Smallcap stocks have staged a sharp rebound over the past two trading sessions, with select constituents of the Nifty Smallcap 100 surging as much as 21.30%. The index has gained over 4% during the period, prompting investors to assess whether the recovery has further legs or whether it is time to book profits.
 Ather Energy led the rally, climbing 21.30% over the last two sessions, followed by Acutaas Chemicals , which gained 20.89%. Onesource Specialty Pharma advanced 19.17%, while Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals rose 16.76%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 16.27%, Sona BLW Precision Forgings advanced 13.15%, and Sterlite Technologies and Himadri Speciality Chemical rose 10.19% and 10.06%, respectively, according to ACE Equities data.
The rally gathered momentum on Tuesday, October 27, with the Nifty Smallcap 100 rising 2.69% to close at 18,468.70. The index has gained 4.31% year-to-date in 2026, even as the benchmark Nifty 50 has declined nearly 13% over the same period.
However, technical analysts have cautioned against interpreting the sharp recovery as confirmation of a sustained turnaround. While buying interest has emerged at lower levels, the index continues to face key resistance levels, making the sustainability of the rebound crucial.
 Should you chase the smallcap rally or book profits?
Jigar S Patel, Senior Manager–Technical Research at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers, said the Nifty Smallcap 100 had witnessed a sharp recovery, indicating buying interest at lower levels. However, he said the broader technical structure continued to warrant caution.
 Live Events
During the previous week's sell-off, the index's daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) slipped below the crucial 30 mark, signalling significant weakness in momentum. The hourly RSI has also yet to cross above 70, indicating that strong bullish momentum is still awaiting confirmation.
“Therefore, despite the recent recovery, the possibility of another pullback cannot be ruled out,” Patel said.
From a technical perspective, 18,000 is the immediate support for the index, followed by 17,600. On the upside, 18,800 is the immediate resistance, while 19,000 is the next hurdle.
A sustained move above these levels, supported by improving RSI momentum, would strengthen the recovery outlook. Until then, Patel advised traders to remain cautious and avoid chasing the rally.
Deepesh Sarawagi, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, said the Nifty Smallcap 100 had rebounded sharply after finding support in the 17,400–17,500 zone, indicating buying interest at lower levels. He sees the recovery extending towards 18,600–18,900, followed by the 19,050–19,200 resistance zone. However, the index continues to trade below its 20-day, 50-day and 100-day exponential moving averages (EMAs), indicating that the broader trend remains under pressure.
The 200-day EMA, near 18,618, is the immediate hurdle, Sarawagi said. A sustained move above this level would strengthen the prospects of a recovery.
The RSI has rebounded to 40.27 from oversold territory, pointing to improving momentum. According to Sarawagi, the rally could extend in the near term, provided the index holds above 18,000–18,200.
He suggested that investors consider partial profit booking near resistance levels while maintaining a cautiously bullish outlook.
 Firstsource, CDSL, PW among top stocks to buy
Sarawagi has further recommended three stocks—Firstsource Solutions, CDSL and Physicswallah—for investors to consider, citing improving technical indicators and signs of a potential recovery.
For Firstsource Solutions (FSL), he has recommended buying at Rs 299, with a target price of Rs 330 and a stop loss of Rs 284. The stock has broken above a downward trendline on the daily chart, supported by volumes, while the bullish crossover of its 20-day EMA above the 200-day EMA and an RSI of 66.64 indicate positive momentum.
For CDSL, Sarawagi has suggested buying at Rs 1,222, with a target of Rs 1,350 and a stop loss of Rs 1,160. The stock has shown signs of recovery after finding support in the Rs 1,150–Rs 1,160 zone and moving above the previous session’s high. Its RSI has rebounded from oversold territory to 38.65, suggesting easing selling pressure.
For Physicswallah (PWL), the analyst has recommended buying at Rs 129.89, with a target price of Rs 147 and a stop loss of Rs 121. The stock has formed a bullish reversal candle near its Rs 120–Rs 123 support zone, rebounded from the rising 200-day EMA and reclaimed its 50-day and 100-day EMAs. Its RSI has also turned upwards to 49.47, indicating that downward pressure may be easing.

 Jio Platforms received as many as three Buy recommendations on the first day of its mega listing as foreign brokerage Nomura, Motilal Oswal and Elara Capital initiated coverage on the stock with a Buy rating.
 Shares of Jio Platforms, the country’s largest public offer to date, listed at Rs 1,358 on the BSE on Wednesday, an impressive 21.36% premium over the IPO price of Rs 1,119 per share. Jio Platforms’ IPO, with an issue size around Rs 30,200 crore, generated cumulative demand of more than Rs 7 lakh crore across the anchor and public book-building process.
The IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening. Its Rs 5,500 crore qualified institutional buyer portion was subscribed within the first 10 minutes. At the close of the third day, the IPO had been subscribed 22.2 times, while the QIB portion was subscribed 70.55 times.
 Why are brokerages bullish on the stock?
Nomura says disruptor is now the leader: International brokerage Nomura initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,340, implying an upside of 20% from the issue price of Rs 1,119.
 Also read: Jio Platforms shares list at 21% premium over IPO price. Should investors buy, sell or hold the stock? 
 Live Events
Jio Platforms, India's largest telecom operator, held a 41.7% share of wireless subscribers, excluding M2M, in August 2026, according to TRAI. With the widest 5G coverage, data usage per subscriber 27% higher than Airtel and the lowest monthly churn rate among peers at 1.6%, Jio is well positioned to narrow its ARPU gap with Airtel, analysts say. A 15% industry-wide tariff hike in November-December 2026 could provide an immediate boost to ARPU.
With most of its 5G investment cycle behind it, Jio's capital expenditure (capex) is expected to decline, falling to around 23% of revenue in FY26 from 35% in FY25, freeing up significant cash flow and driving a sharp improvement in free cash flow (FCF). Nomura says Jio Platforms’ balance sheet is also strengthening, with net debt-to-equity, including deferred payment obligations, declining from 0.56 times in FY24 to 0.37 times in FY26. Nomura expects Jio to become debt-free on a net basis by FY29.
Jio is the gateway to digital India: Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal started coverage with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,350, an upside of 21% from the IPO price.
“Reliance Jio’s entry into the Indian telecom industry was a seminal event, which changed the rules of the game from minutes to megabytes, forcing the sector to consolidate from 12+ telcos before RJio’s launch to a 3+1 market structure,” the brokerage said.
 Read more: Jio Platforms shares to be available under MTF from Day 1. What should investors know? 
Motilal Oswal projects a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14% in revenue, 15% in reported EBITDA and 20% in profit after tax (PAT) for Jio Platforms (JPL) over FY26-29. Growth is expected to be driven by strong subscriber additions, the impact of around 15% tariff hikes from March 2027, continued expansion of the home broadband subscriber base and the scaling up of digital platform offerings.
Motilal Oswal expects capex to remain range-bound at Rs 340-360 billion over the medium term, supporting cumulative free cash flow (FCF) generation over FY26-29, after interest and lease payments. Strong FCF generation and IPO proceeds are expected to help Jio become a net cash company by FY29.
At the IPO price and current market price (CMP), Jio is valued at par with Bharti Airtel's India business, excluding Indus and Bharti Airtel's minority interests, based on Motilal Oswal's estimates.
The brokerage believes Jio could command a premium to Bharti Airtel's India business in the near term, supported by its market leadership, greater influence over industry tariffs and a free float of less than 3%. However, its earnings and valuation estimates remain highly sensitive to growth in wireless average revenue per user (ARPU).
 Also read: Ambani pulls off a blockbuster: Jio IPO makes 13 records, rewrites Dalal Street history 
Jio’s digital springboard is affordability: Elara Capital has initiated coverage of Jio Platforms with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,367 per share. Mobility will remain the primary driver of revenue and profitability, with the brokerage expecting subscriber additions to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 3% during FY26-29E, supported by affordable plans, an extensive network and low churn.
It also expects a tariff hike of 12-15% from H2FY27E. Along with 2G-to-4G and 5G migration, prepaid-to-postpaid upgrades, premiumisation, higher data consumption and bundled digital services, this is expected to drive average revenue per user (ARPU) from Rs 214 in FY26 to Rs 257 in FY29E.
Affordable data remains the foundation of Jio Platforms' ecosystem for consumers and enterprises. The company leverages its customer base and distribution platforms to integrate third-party services, reduce customer acquisition costs and deepen engagement. India's underpenetrated digital services market presents a structural growth opportunity across enterprise cloud, communications and consumer productivity solutions.
Speaking at Jio’s blockbuster listing on stock exchanges, Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said the company’s next phase would focus on “democratising every technology that can transform lives,” including AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity from space and digital services yet to be imagined.

docs.title: Weak domestic returns fuel India's overseas retail investing boom
docs.text:
India's top money managers are launching a flurry of funds in a tax-neutral hub to absorb the record sums that domestic investors are sending overseas, frustrated by weak returns at home and craving exposure to AI-related assets.
 At least half a dozen such funds have been launched in the past six months, including the JioBlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund this week by the joint venture of Mukesh Ambani's Jio Financial and BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager.
The overseas investment rush poses a dilemma for policymakers, who have spent years encouraging households to move savings from real estate, gold and bank deposits into domestic equities.
The world's most populous nation has more than 130 million retail stock investors, many of whom are scouring for investment targets abroad, from New York to Kazakhstan, after sustained underperformance in the domestic stock market.
"Over the last two years, we've seen a clear increase in demand for global assets," said Shobhit Mathur, co-founder of money manager Ionic Asset. "Investors are no longer looking at overseas exposure as a tactical allocation but increasingly as a permanent part of portfolio construction."
 Live Events
International investments by individuals in India either directly or through funds more than doubled from a year earlier to nearly $2.3 billion in the first half of 2026, on track to surpass the 2025 full year's record $2.65 billion, data from the central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), showed.
One such investor is Ankit Khandelwal, a 41-year-old resident of Kota in the western Indian state of Rajasthan who invests in global exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and companies listed in markets such as Kazakhstan and Mongolia.
"It began as an experiment but since then better returns overseas and persistent rupee weakness has led me to grow the overseas portion of my portfolio to over 60% from about 5% in early 2025," said Khandelwal, who is an import and export adviser to companies, adding that he understands metals, mining and energy firms of the world.
India's rupee currency hit a record low this year as its stock market suffered sustained selling by institutional investors and as its economy was hit by rising energy costs from the Iran war. The South Asian nation caps overseas remittances at an annual $250,000 per person because its currency is not fully convertible.
The benchmark Nifty 50 index is down 5.3% over the last two years, compared with a 47% gain in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index and a 32% rise in the S&P 500 in the US.
High valuations and a lack of AI-related stocks have also weighed on returns from local equities.
Little wonder then that retail trading account openings for domestic investments fell by a quarter to 33 million in the fiscal year ending March 2026, data from Indian depositories showed.
 Gift City
The RBI restricts Indian funds to a maximum cumulative overseas investment of $7 billion and a $1 billion limit for an individual asset manager. With the limits almost exhausted, funds cannot create fresh units to invest at will even as demand grows.
But these limits do not apply to overseas investment funds of domestic asset managers launched through the GIFT City tax-neutral hub located in India's western Gujarat state.
Thus, besides JioBlackRock, HDFC Asset Management, Parag Parikh and Aditya Birla Sun Life have launched such funds in the last six months.
Other domestic funds that invest in foreign equities too are sought after, despite the RBI limits. Assets in overseas fund-of-funds schemes rose 42% year-on-year to 488 billion rupees in September, while investors registered for such investments climbed 34% to nearly 2 million, according to data published by the Association of Mutual Funds in India.
The paucity of overseas investment avenues for Indian investors has driven some overseas ETFs to trade at hefty premiums to their net asset values.
One such fund, the Motilal Oswal Nasdaq Q50 ETF, traded as much as 65% to 80% above the value of its underlying portfolio at times in September, while some Mirae Asset overseas ETFs commanded premiums of 27% to 58%.
 Regulators Cautious
Retail investors are also racing to gain direct exposure to US and other overseas stocks, with discount brokers Groww , Zerodha and Angel One launching fractional investing platforms this month.
Similar investment trends are underway in a number of markets, including China, where regulators have tightened scrutiny of unofficial channels through which money is being sent overseas.
Indian authorities are cautious about the money flowing abroad from such investments but are not considering measures to curb such flows, three people at Indian regulators told Reuters.
Emails to India's market regulator and the RBI, which sets overseas investment limits, were not answered.
Some industry executives voiced caution.
"Indian markets have not given returns and overseas markets are looking attractive," said Swarup Mohanty, chief executive of Mirae Asset Investment Managers. "If you want to invest for diversification then it's fine, but investing purely to chase short-term returns is worrying."

 Several mutual fund houses have temporarily stopped accepting fresh investments into gold fund-of-funds (FoFs), leaving investors wondering whether they can continue investing through existing SIPs and what alternatives are available. Here is what the restrictions mean and what investors can do if they still want exposure to gold.
 WHAT ARE GOLD FUND-OF-FUNDS (FOFs), AND HOW DO THEY WORK?
Gold FoFs are mutual fund schemes that invest in Gold ETFs rather than buying physical gold directly.
When an investor puts money into a Gold FoF, the fund manager uses that money to purchase units of a Gold ETF. The Gold ETF, in turn, invests in physical gold. As a result, a Gold FoF’s value generally moves in line with gold prices. 
They offer a simple way to invest in gold through the mutual fund route without needing a demat account. Investors can buy and redeem units like any other mutual fund scheme while gaining exposure to changes in gold prices.
 WHY HAVE SOME MUTUAL FUND HOUSES RESTRICTED FRESH INVESTMENTS IN GOLD FOFs?
Several fund houses have temporarily stopped accepting fresh investments in Gold FoFs from mid-October. The restrictions include fresh lump-sum investments, new SIP registrations and switch-ins, though they differ across schemes.
 Live Events
While fund houses have not disclosed specific reasons behind the move, industry participants believe it may be linked to concerns over rising gold imports and strong inflows into gold investment products. As these ETF units are backed by physical gold, sustained inflows into such products can translate into higher demand for imported gold.
 Read more: Best gilt mutual funds to invest in October 2026 
 CAN’T INVEST IN A GOLD FOF? WHAT ARE THE OTHER OPTIONS?
Gold ETFs are one of the closest alternatives for investors seeking exposure to gold through market-linked investments. While there are restrictions on fresh investments in several Gold FoFs, there are none on their ETFs.
 Read more: Top 8 equity MFs offer double-digit gains on SIP investments since last Diwali. Do you own any? 
 HOW ARE GOLD ETFs DIFFERENT FROM GOLD FOFs?
Gold FoFs are generally more convenient for retail investors because they can be bought and redeemed like any other mutual fund scheme without requiring a demat account. Gold ETFs can only be bought and sold through a demat and trading account.
Gold ETFs typically have lower costs because investors bear only the ETF’s expense ratio. In a Gold FoF, investors indirectly bear the expenses of both the FoF and the underlying ETF.
Liquidity also differs. Gold ETFs can be bought and sold on stock exchanges during market hours, while Gold FoFs are purchased and redeemed at the day’s closing net asset value (NAV), like regular mutual funds.
However, unlike Gold FoFs, their ETFs do not offer the convenience of a mutual fund SIP. Though many brokers have SIP facilities for buying ETFs and stocks, they are perceived to be relatively less user-friendly. Also, not all ETFs are liquid. Some of them might be trading at a premium to the ETF’s NAV.

docs.title: Gold dips on firmer dollar; US inflation data in focus
docs.text:
Gold slipped on Thursday as the dollar firmed, while investors assessed policy signals from the Federal Reserve and Chair Kevin Warsh after the central bank left interest rates unchanged and awaited key US inflation data due later in the day.
 Fundamentals
Spot gold fell 0.7% to $4,039.26 per ounce by 0044 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery steadied at $4,051.00.
The dollar held firm, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.
The Fed held rates steady on Wednesday as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections while it awaits further data on inflation, which the central bank said "remains elevated."
Traders are pricing in about a 78% chance of a rate hike in December, compared with 84% before the announcement, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.
 Live Events
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
Markets are awaiting the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data due at 1230 GMT, a key gauge closely watched by the Fed as it targets a 2% inflation rate.
The European Central Bank is set to keep rates on hold on Thursday in a well-telegraphed decision that is likely to be overshadowed by questions about bond-market turmoil in France.
Global commodity prices are set to surge 23% in 2026, the World Bank said on Wednesday, citing rising energy prices and disruptions to cargo shipping during the Middle East war, grain shipment problems in the Black Sea and high demand for safe-haven assets such as gold.
China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in September rose more than 28% from August to a five-month high, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Wednesday.
On the geopolitical front, Yemen's Houthis attacked Aden airport on Wednesday, Yemeni government forces said, after the Iran-aligned group warned people to evacuate the facility as fighting escalated in the impoverished country caught in the wider Middle East conflict.
Spot silver slid 0.7% to $53.60 per ounce, platinum dropped 0.3% to $1,533.50 and palladium gained 0.7% to $1,017.29.

docs.title: HUL sales rise 15% to hit 14-quarter high, but inflation clouds demand outlook
docs.text:
Mumbai: Hindustan Unilever , India's consumer-goods bellwether, reported its strongest underlying sales growth in 14 quarters in the three months to September, but cautioned that elevated commodity inflation and below-normal monsoon rains could affect the pace of broader consumption recovery. HUL's turnover rose 15% to ₹18,071 crore in the September quarter, while underlying volume growth was 7%, despite price increases of about 7.5%. Net profit was flat at ₹2,796 crore, reflecting a one-off tax-related gain of ₹273 crore in the year-earlier period.
 The Surf Excel-maker expects demand to remain resilient, though persistent inflation and pockets of rural stress remain key challenges for the industry in the coming months.
 Also Read: Hindustan Unilever to take calibrated price hikes as commodity inflation stays high, says CEO Priya Nair 
 Segmental Breakdown 
"Essentials have a low putdown price. So, at an overall level, these products tend to be less elastic to pricing as compared with other more discretionary categories. The fact that there is volume momentum while we are taking price increases is a very good sign for overall demand," said Priya Nair, managing director, HUL. "We have taken a significant price hike of 7.5% and yet we are seeing momentum sequentially on volumes."
 Live Events
 India's largest consumer goods maker, considered a proxy for consumption demand in the country, said sales in both urban and rural markets remained positive, with rural demand increasing sequentially.
 HUL also welcomed the package labelling requirements proposed by food safety watchdog FSSAI, saying they would enhance transparency, and that it would comply with all norms.
Unilever CEO Fernando Fernandez said India lapped a GST-led lower prior year comparator but saw significant share gains. "Our performance in India is boosted by significant share gains in our main categories, particularly in beauty laundry that are our two largest categories there. So, there is a bit of health from the market, but also our performance," Fernandez told analysts.
The broader rural outlook, however, remains patchy as rainfall deficits threaten agricultural output and incomes in some regions. Responding to concerns about the impact of the below-normal monsoon, Nair said, "The question is of wages, and really what happens to rural wages?"
 Also Read: Hindustan Unilever Limited backs FSSAI labelling norms for food products high in fat, salt and sugar 
She pointed to government support measures as potential cushions. "The MSP (minimum support price) has been taken up by 5% to 6% by the government, so that's a very good move. The other is we are seeing a higher (G-RAM-G) outlay, so there will be a cushioning of rural wages in the pockets that you know is a challenge," she said.
 Encouraging Indicators 
Nair cited India's 7.8% GDP growth in the June quarter and positive high-frequency indicators, including electricity demand, GST revenues and passenger vehicle sales, as signs of economic resilience. But she said "there are pockets of challenge" and that "inflation is the key challenge that you know everyone's looking at."
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 8% to Rs4,089 crore. Margin was 22.6%, down 140 basis points year on year.
"We will always cover costs. We will ensure that we do the right savings programs, the right efficiencies. But our focus is to deliver volume-led revenue and profit growth. So absolute profit growth is very important for us to also look at. That's really how our algorithm is structured," Nair added.
HUL chief finance officer Niranjan Gupta said it expects commodity inflation to remain elevated in the short term but the company is confident of keeping its medium-term EBITDA margin within the guided range of 22% to 24%.
Homecare was the fastest-growing segment, with underlying sales growth of 22% and revenue of Rs6,878 crore. Double-digit growth across fabric wash and household care helped offset pressure from petrochemical-linked inputs. The segment's operating margin fell to 16% from 19% a year earlier. "To have taken a 10% price increase and still deliver 10% underlying volume growth in a category like home care actually depicts the strength of our brand and the resilience of our portfolio," Gupta added.
Beauty and wellbeing revenue grew 16% to Rs4,319 crore, supported by double-digit volume growth in hair care, skincare and colour cosmetics. Personal care revenue rose 9% to Rs2,617 crore, but volumes were flat. Skin cleansing delivered double-digit growth, supported by pricing and volume growth in Dove and Pears bars, while oral care recorded low-single-digit growth.
The food segmental revenue increased 9% to Rs3,849 crore, with low-single-digit volume growth. Tea remained under pressure, particularly at the mass-market end, as inflation weighed on performance.

docs.title: Karnataka, DGFT to host state-level workshop to help exporters leverage FTAs
docs.text:
Bengaluru: The Office of the Additional Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Bengaluru, in partnership with the Karnataka government and the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), will host a state-level workshop on October 30 at The Lalit Ashok to help local businesses capitalise on India’s Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), according to a Press Information Bureau (PIB) release.
 The outreach initiative aims to boost Karnataka’s export competitiveness and expand international market access by driving awareness and effective utilisation of trade pacts, particularly recently concluded agreements.
Karnataka Minister for Large and Medium Industries MB Patil is scheduled to inaugurate the event and address exporters, alongside senior officials from both the Union and state governments. 
Nearly 200 participants are expected to attend, including prominent state exporters, officials from District Industries Centres (DICs), Export Promotion Council (EPC) representatives, and industry stakeholders.
Technical sessions will feature presentations by Abhay Sinha, Director General of the Services Export Promotion Council, on services-sector opportunities, and Tamanna Chaturvedi, Trade Advisor at the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), on emerging avenues and policy interventions for Karnataka under new FTAs.
 Live Events
The release added that the workshop will also feature dedicated sectoral discussions to pinpoint export potential and practical solutions across four focus areas: agriculture, dairy, marine products and food processing; textiles, apparel and made-ups; engineering, electronics and semiconductors; and services.

docs.title: South Korea updates international education reforms; introduces incentives to develop Korean language skil
docs.text:
Synopsis
 South Korea aims to change its international student visa system by focusing on Korean language proficiency and academic performance. The Ministry of Justice outlined plans to allow students with intermediate Korean skills to obtain visas without financial proofs. Proposed regulations will affect part-time work eligibility based on language achievements and could require language proficiency for visa extensions.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 South Korea is planning changes to its international student visa system, with greater emphasis on Korean language proficiency as the country targets 400,000 foreign students.
The Ministry of Justice has announced the decisions of the Consultative Council on the Improvement of the Foreign Student Visa System . Established in April, the council is tasked with developing strategies to support the country's international student target. It is chaired by Acting Justice Minister Jinsoo Lee and includes experts in higher education and immigration.
Also read: New Zealand updates student visa regulations, reducing research students' work rights significantly 
South Korea achieved its target of 300,000 international students two years ahead of schedule, in mid-2025. Foreign student enrolments reached 314,000 in February 2026.
The proposed changes aim to help international students succeed academically and integrate into Korean society, while supporting the government's plans to increase foreign enrolments.
 Korean language skills linked to visa requirements 
Under the proposed framework, most international students who demonstrate intermediate Korean language proficiency could obtain study visas without having to prove their financial means.
Students would need to achieve Level 4 in either the Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK) or the Korean Immigration and Integration Program (KIIP).
However, students considered at high risk of overstaying their visas or prioritising employment over their studies could be required to use the Study Expense Security Deposit System. This requires them to deposit funds to cover living expenses for a specified period while studying in South Korea.
Korean language proficiency and academic performance would also determine whether international students can work part-time. Students would need at least Level 3 in TOPIK to qualify under the proposed criteria.
Also read: New visa rules for Australian students may force some international students to apply from overseas 
 Rules for international graduates 
Language skills would also influence how long international graduates can remain in South Korea after completing their studies. 
Under the planned framework, graduates could be permitted to stay for between one and three years, depending on their Korean proficiency and their preparation for employment.
The government is also considering a new visa, tentatively named the Korean Study Alumni Visitor Visa , to encourage international graduates in selected fields to maintain links with the country.
These fields include science and engineering, manufacturing and specialised technical occupations. Graduates with relevant qualifications could receive priority consideration for a Skilled Worker (E-7) visa, provided they meet the Korean language requirements.
 English-taught courses could face a challenge 
The proposed emphasis on Korean language proficiency could create difficulties for students who choose South Korea primarily for English-language degrees or its cultural attractions.
Achieving TOPIK Level 4 or the equivalent KIIP qualification can require years of intensive study. Under the planned framework, students may need this level to qualify for an exemption from financial proof, while Level 3 would be required for part-time work.
However, English-taught courses have helped South Korea attract international students. More than 1,000 departments across over 70 universities offer degrees in English, providing options for students who do not have advanced Korean language skills.
The proposed changes reflect the government's attempt to balance further growth in international enrolments with students' academic performance, social integration and employment prospects. The language requirements could support students who intend to build careers in South Korea, but may also influence the choices of those seeking an English-language education.

docs.title: US agency approves Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion acquisition of Globalstar
docs.text:
Synopsis
 The Federal Communications Commission said Tuesday it has approved Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion deal to acquire Globalstar as the retail giant's satellite arm aims to build a satellite-based communications network to take on Elon Musk's SpaceX Starlink unit.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 The Federal Communications Commission said Tuesday it has approved Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion deal to acquire Globalstar as the retail giant's satellite arm aims to build a satellite-based communications network to take on Elon Musk's SpaceX Starlink unit.
Amazon Leo has launched more than 300 satellites since April 2025 and aims to deploy about 3,200 satellites in Earth's low orbit by 2029. Through the deal, Amazon adds Globalstar's two dozen satellites to its existing network of more than 200 and its mobile-satellite spectrum. Amazon, which has committed to investing more than $10 billion in Leo, is preparing to roll out its commercial satellite services by the end of 2026, the FCC said.
The FCC said the companies' assets will boost Amazon Leo's entry into the direct-to-device market and allow the satellite-operator to offer fixed and mobile services. 
"The FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country," FCC Chair Brendan Carr said.
Direct-to-device satellite ​technology allows smartphones and other devices to connect directly to satellites.
Tech companies are pouring billions of ‌dollars into capturing the lucrative market for satellite-based connectivity as they race to complete with Starlink's network of more than 11,000 satellites.
The FCC will vote Thursday to advance a new auction of wireless spectrum to boost "direct-to-device" services.
Globalstar currently powers satellite-based safety features such as Emergency SOS and Find My for Apple's iPhone and Apple Watch ​users. Amazon said earlier that it has signed an agreement with Apple to continue providing those services.
Apple invested about $1.5 billion in Globalstar in 2024 to fund the expansion of its iPhone communication ‌services, in ⁠a deal that also gave the tech giant a 20% equity in Globalstar. Apple accounted for about 63% of Globalstar revenue last year and Amazon plans to acquire Apple's stake, the FCC said.
Globalstar said late last year that a new, Apple-backed network under development would expand its footprint to 54 satellites, including a small number of backups, from the two dozen currently.

docs.title: Centre releases Rs 78 crore for senior citizens' welfare scheme
docs.text:
New Delhi: The Centre has released Rs 77.98 crore in grant-in-aid for 755 projects under its senior citizens' welfare scheme for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, the Social Justice and Empowerment Ministry said on Wednesday.
 The ministry said it has released funds under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), a component of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), for the financial year 2026-27.
Launched in 2021, AVYAY is a flagship scheme of the ministry that promotes "ageing with dignity" and "ageing in place" by ensuring older persons can live with respect, security, and independence. 
The ministry said the assistance aims to strengthen service delivery and welfare interventions for senior citizens through institutional care and related facilities.
With India's senior citizen population projected to reach 23 crore by 2036, the need for comprehensive and accessible support systems is growing. The scheme seeks to address this demographic challenge by strengthening institutional mechanisms and encouraging community participation, it said.
 Live Events
According to the 2011 Census, India had 10.38 crore people aged 60 years and above, including 5.11 crore males and 5.27 crore females.
The Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) highlights functional limitations among a substantial proportion of older persons, underscoring the need for reliable care, healthcare services and community-based support, the ministry said.
Increasing urbanisation, migration and the growth of nuclear households are also changing traditional family support structures, making institutional and community-based care increasingly important for senior citizens, it added.
AVYAY subsumed and expanded the earlier National Action Plan for Senior Citizens (NAPSrC), bringing multiple interventions for older persons under a unified scheme.
The scheme aims to provide shelter, food, healthcare and recreational services while strengthening the capacities of governments, non-governmental organisations, local bodies and communities to support older persons.
The "ageing in place" approach promotes an environment where senior citizens can continue living safely in their homes and communities, supported by suitable home modifications and specialised community-based services where needed, the ministry said.
The scheme combines institutional assistance, state-level planning, and district-level monitoring, focusing on the dignity, well-being, independence, and social inclusion of older persons.
Under the State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) component, state and Union Territory governments prepare and implement welfare action plans tailored to their respective requirements, with financial support from the ministry.

 Chasing a target of 132, India reached 133 for two in just 17 overs. Pratika remained unbeaten on 59 off 56 balls, while Shafali scored an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls.
Earlier, left-arm spinner Vaishnavi led India's bowling attack with figures of 5/39, dismantling Zimbabwe's top and middle order. Kranti Gaud and Sayali Satghare picked up two wickets each as Zimbabwe were bowled out in 39.5 overs. 
Opening batter and wicketkeeper Modester Mupachikwa was Zimbabwe's top scorer with 37 runs, while captain Josephine Nkomo contributed 35.
India had won the first two matches by nine wickets and 121 runs, respectively.

docs.title: Assam Rifles DG reviews India-Myanmar border security, fencing work in Manipur
docs.text:
Guwahati: Assam Rifles Director General Lieutenant General Vikas Lakhera reviewed border security arrangements and the progress of fencing work along the India-Myanmar border in the state.
 Assam Rifles sources said that, as part of a continuing operational review in Manipur , the Assam Rifles Director General visited Moreh and Chongjang in Tengnoupal district, which shares a border with Myanmar.
Lt General Lakhera inspected key border crossing points and interacted with local residents. He emphasised the importance of effective surveillance, heightened operational preparedness and robust border management to ensure sustained vigilance and security in the region. 
Manipur Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla last week reviewed the progress of the ongoing India-Myanmar border fencing work at a meeting with senior officials.
Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh recently stressed the need for stronger management of the long international border, better surveillance systems and joint action against drug trafficking, arms smuggling and human trafficking at a NITI Aayog meeting in New Delhi.
 Live Events
An Assam Rifles official said that Lt General Lakhera met state Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla at Lok Bhavan in Imphal on Tuesday. “The interaction focused on the prevailing security situation, operational preparedness and ongoing efforts towards maintaining peace and stability in the state. The meeting underscored the importance of continued coordination and collective efforts to foster lasting peace and security in Manipur.

docs.title: WPL 2027 Auction: G Kamalini goes to Gujarat Giants for Rs 40 lakh, Kiran Navgire joins Delhi Capitals for
docs.text:
Delhi Capitals signed Kiran Navgire for Rs 75 lakh and Gujarat Giants picked up young batter G Kamalini for Rs 40 lakh as the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 mini-auction began in Kochi on Wednesday.
 Navgire was Delhi Capitals’ first signing of the auction. Kamalini went to Gujarat Giants at her base price, with no rival bid.
Navgire, who was earlier part of UP Warriorz, had a base price of Rs 40 lakh. Mumbai Indians opened the bidding for her. Delhi Capitals then joined in, and the two franchises pushed her price up to Rs 70 lakh. 
 Also read: WPL 2027 auction: UP Warriorz pick Sushma Verma for Rs 30 lakh as Uma Chetry, Taniya Bhatia go unsold 
Delhi Capitals raised the bid to Rs 75 lakh, after which Mumbai Indians withdrew from the race.
 Live Events
 Kamalini goes at base price 
Kamalini is a wicketkeeper-batter with a modest WPL record so far. She has scored heavily for India A and Tamil Nadu in domestic cricket. Gujarat Giants opened the bidding at Rs 40 lakh, and no other team entered the race, ANI reported.
 Big names go unsold 
Several players failed to find a buyer. Raghvi Bist, who has played two T20 Internationals for India, was the first player to go under the hammer. She went unsold at her base price of Rs 30 lakh.
Ayushi Soni also went unsold at Rs 30 lakh. She has played one T20 International and one WPL match in 2025.
England’s Sophia Dunkley, who set the highest base price of Rs 50 lakh, found no buyer either. She played six matches for Gujarat Giants in the first WPL season.
Maharashtra batter Tejal Hasabnis also went unsold. She is known for her big hitting in the middle order and plays alongside Smriti Mandhana for Maharashtra. She is part of India’s ODI squad for the ongoing series against Zimbabwe.
A total of 146 players are in the pool for just 27 slots across the five teams. Of these, 20 are for Indian players and seven for overseas players.
The money is tight. Before the auction, UP Warriorz had the biggest purse at Rs 3.75 crore with eight slots to fill. Mumbai Indians had the smallest at Rs 90 lakh, with six slots and none for overseas players.
Other names in the pool include Indian cricketers Sneh Rana and Sushma Verma, and Australians Grace Harris, Jess Jonassen and Sophie Molineux. The fifth WPL season is scheduled from January 14 to February 7, 2027.

docs.title: Rahul Gandhi politicising commercial and legal matters: Nirmala Sitharaman
docs.text:
New Delhi: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday accused leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi of politicising commercial and legal matters after he commented on an internal tussle within the Tata group . "Casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable," Sitharaman said on X.
 She was responding to Gandhi's post that said, "Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word. How long will you stay silent? Until they own you? Indian business is not Modi and Shah's plaything. You lack courage. We don't. We will ensure justice for these crimes."
Sitharaman said the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi values Indian industry as job creators and drivers of economic growth. 
 Read more: Rahul Gandhi responds to FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tata row, seeks answers on meeting at Amit Shah’s residence 
"Our policies have been tailored to enable enterprise, support industry and encourage investment," she said.
 Live Events
The finance minister said that Gandhi has repeatedly decried the successes of Indian industry and entrepreneurs. "Now, are you trying to incite our business leaders to join you in spreading distrust and toxicity?" she said in her post. "For decades, your (Congress) party had smothered the spirit of the Indian entrepreneurs under the stifling 'Licence-Quota Raj' and inflicted poverty on crores of Indians," she alleged.
Gandhi's comments came in the backdrop of a tussle involving Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran.
Later, responding to Sitharaman, the Congress leader posted on X: "Which 'legal and commercial matter' required Tata Trusts and Tata Sons to be hosted at Amit Shah's residence?"
He further alleged: "When is crony number 1 going to appear in the game and which piece of Tata is he going to get?... Finally, all India's businesses except 3-4 of your cronies, already hate all of you and don't need any incitement."
Sitharaman, in her post, said political parties, leaders, governments and institutions share an equal responsibility to support industry, strengthen farmers and secure the future of youth. "Therefore, it is essential to engage constructively rather than casting baseless aspersions to suit your narrow political motives," she said.
The minister further said the Constitution of India ensures justice to all its citizens. "History is witness to the shoddy manner in which you, your party and the PMs belonging to your party have demeaned the judiciary. So Rahul ji, refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere," she added.

Additionally, it has breached the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the prior up move from 24,571 to 26,341, he added. As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

 Jio Platforms listing gain: Motilal Oswal initiates Buy with Rs 1,350 target, sees upside from digital growth
 Motilal Oswal has initiated coverage on Jio Platforms with a Buy rating and Rs 1,350 target price, implying 21 percent upside from its IPO price. The brokerage expects tariff hikes, broadband expansion and improving free cash flow to drive growth.
 Shaleen Agrawal 
 October 28, 2026 / 09:50 IST 
 --> 
 Jio Platforms 
 Motilal Oswal initiates Jio Platforms with Buy rating.
 Target price set at Rs 1,350 per share with 21% upside.
 Jio Platforms scheduled to debut on BSE and NSE on Oct 28.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Brokerage firm Motilal Oswal Financial Services has initiated coverage on Reliance Industries-backed Jio Platforms with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,350 per share, implying 21 percent upside from its IPO issue price of Rs 1,119. The brokerage expects tariff hikes, strong subscriber additions, home broadband expansion and growing digital services to drive earnings growth over the next three years.
In its report titled ‘The gateway of digital India!’, Motilal Oswal projected a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 14 percent in Jio Platforms' consolidated revenue, 15 percent in reported EBITDA and 20 percent in net profit between FY26 and FY29.
The brokerage expects Jio Platforms to generate cumulative free cash flow of Rs 1.46 lakh crore over FY26-29 and achieve a net cash position by FY29, supported by improving profitability, moderating capital expenditure and IPO proceeds.
Jio Platforms shares are scheduled to make their stock market debut on the BSE and NSE on Wednesday, October 28, following its Rs 30,188-crore IPO, which was subscribed 22.19 times.
Motilal Oswal expects Reliance Jio to benefit from an approximately 15 percent smartphone tariff hike in March 2027, alongside continued subscriber additions.
The brokerage estimates India's wireless telecom industry revenue will grow at a CAGR of around 10 percent to Rs 4 lakh crore by FY29.
Reliance Jio currently commands approximately 41.4 percent of India's wireless subscribers and 42.3 percent of wireless revenue. Motilal Oswal expects its wireless revenue market share to rise to 43.3 percent by FY29.
The brokerage projects an 11 percent CAGR in Reliance Jio's wireless revenue and 13 percent in EBITDA over FY26-29.
Motilal Oswal identified home broadband as a major growth driver for Reliance Jio, which currently serves around 3 crore broadband subscribers.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
The brokerage expects Jio to account for approximately 73 percent of incremental industry home broadband subscriber additions between FY26 and FY29, taking its subscriber base to around 5 crore.
It forecasts a 27 percent CAGR in home broadband revenue over the period, with the segment's contribution to Reliance Jio's revenue increasing to around 12 percent by FY29 from approximately 8 percent currently.
Beyond connectivity, Motilal Oswal sees opportunities in cloud services, enterprise communications, Internet of Things (IoT), managed services and international partnerships involving Jio's proprietary telecom technology.
Motilal Oswal values Jio Platforms at 11.5 times estimated FY29 reported EBITDA, arriving at an equity valuation of Rs 12.4 lakh crore and a target price of Rs 1,350.
The brokerage believes Jio Platforms could trade at a premium to Bharti Airtel's India business over the near term, supported by its market leadership, greater influence over telecom tariffs and limited free float of less than 3 percent.
Its bull-case target stands at Rs 1,690, while the bear-case target is Rs 1,035.
However, the brokerage flagged delays in tariff hikes, increased competition, higher capital expenditure and slower digital services growth as key risks to its estimates.

 Nomura has initiated coverage on Jio Platforms with a Buy rating and Rs 1,340 target price, implying nearly 20 percent upside from its IPO price. The brokerage expects tariff hikes, home broadband growth and improving free cash flow to drive long-term value creation.
 Shaleen Agrawal

 Jio Platforms 
 Nomura initiates Jio Platforms with Buy and target of Rs 1,340.
 Brokerage expects steady tariff hikes and home broadband growth.
 Jio shares to debut on October 28 following record IPO.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Japanese brokerage Nomura has initiated coverage of Jio Platforms with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,340 per share, implying nearly 20 percent upside from the IPO price of Rs 1,119.
The brokerage expects steady tariff hikes, growth in home broadband, and improving free cash flow to support the telecom company's performance as its shares debut on October 28.
Nomura said Jio, once the disruptor, is now the leader, highlighting its dominant position in India’s telecom market, with a 42 percent share of wireless subscribers, 60 percent of data traffic, and 43 percent of home broadband. The brokerage expects Jio's listing to encourage the company, which it describes as a price setter, to pursue steady tariff increases that other telecom operators could follow.
Nomura estimates Jio Platforms ' EBITDA will grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.5 percent between FY26 and FY29.
Nomura identified home broadband as Jio's second growth engine, supported by its extensive network infrastructure and market leadership.
The brokerage also expects a sharp improvement in free cash flow (FCF) as capital expenditure intensity declines, with the bulk of Jio's 5G-related investments largely completed. According to Nomura, Jio's strong network and leading subscriber market share position the company for long-term value creation.
At the IPO press conference earlier this month, Managing Director Akash Ambani outlined Jio's strategy to increase revenue realisation per customer by introducing additional digital services rather than relying solely on higher data tariffs.
Ambani said Jio could raise prices but wanted to deliver more services to customers and charge for the added value. He cited the company's voice AI service as an example of revenue opportunities beyond its conventional licensed telecom business.
Jio is also exploring international expansion through a capital expenditure-light model, offering its proprietary telecom technology to overseas operators as a managed services partner.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Jio Platforms shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on Wednesday, following the completion of India's largest IPO. The Rs 30,188-crore public issue was subscribed 22.19 times, with combined demand across the public issue and anchor investor placement exceeding Rs 7.4 lakh crore. The offering attracted nearly 1.39 crore applications.
The company finalised its IPO issue price at Rs 1,119 per share, the upper end of the price band, implying an equity valuation of approximately Rs 10.3 lakh crore. The listing is expected to place Jio Platforms among India’s three largest listed companies by market capitalisation.
Jio Platforms has earmarked up to Rs 27,500 crore of its net IPO proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Ambani said at the IPO press conference that Jio was heading towards becoming net debt-free.

docs.title: Nomura retains Buy rating on Jindal Steel, target price set at Rs 1,300
docs.text: Nomura has retained its Buy rating on Jindal Steel with a target price of Rs 1,300 after Q2FY27 consolidated EBITDA beat its forecast and Bloomberg consensus by 15% and 11%, respectively.Consolidated EBITDA stood at Rs 25 billion, with the beat against Nomuras estimate driven by higher-than-expected realisations. Realisation per tonne improved 12% quarter-on-quarter and was 4% above estimates, supported by better realisations and a higher share of flats in the product mix. Volumes rose 27% year-on-year to 2.4 million tonnes, helped by the ramp-up of the Angul blast furnace.Raw-material cost per tonne increased 1% sequentially, in line with expectations. Conversion costs rose 7% quarter-on-quarter and were 7% above Nomuras estimate, driven by higher power, fuel and freight costs. EBITDA per tonne stood at Rs 10,522, down more than Rs 1,453 sequentially, but the decline was lower than the brokerages forecast of Rs 2,600 per tonne.Jindal expects coking coal prices to rise around $20-25 per tonne in Q3FY27, although prices have recently stabilised. The company also indicated that switching downstream reheating furnaces and processing lines from propane to syngas would generate fuel-cost savings. Propane prices were around Rs 100 per kg, compared with syngas costs of approximately Rs 30 per kg.Value-added products accounted for 57% of the product mix in Q2. Management reiterated its FY27 production target of around 11 million tonnes, including 6 million tonnes in the second half, and a product mix target of 65% flats and 35% longs, compared with the current mix of around 60:40.The company is targeting commissioning of a 2-million-tonne DRI plant, a new pellet plant and three additional gasifiers by June 2027. FY27 capital expenditure guidance remains Rs 75-100 billion, with around Rs 34 billion spent in the first half. Net debt declined Rs 11 billion sequentially to Rs 147.8 billion.Nomura values the stock at 8.5 times target EV/EBITDA. The stock trades at 7.6 times one-year forward EV/EBITDA.

docs.text:
Markets 
 Stock recommendations for 29 October from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 11 min read 29 Oct 2026, 06:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 29 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Stock market recap: Benchmark indices fell on Wednesday, as selling in IT stocks and Reliance Industries weighed on sentiment amid rising crude oil prices and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision.
 The Sensex closed at 73,246.03, down 352.64 points, or 0.48%, while the Nifty fell 50.90 points, or 0.22%, to settle at 22,698.85.
 Broader markets, however, advanced on selective buying. The BSE SmallCap Select index rose 0.85%, while the MidCap Select index gained 0.66%.
 Shares of Jio Platforms , the Reliance Industries-backed digital services company, made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday. The stock ended nearly 27% above its issue price of ₹ 1,119, making Jio Platforms India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries, with a market capitalisation of about ₹ 13 trillion.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: TVS Motor Co. Ltd (current price: ₹ 4240) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong EV (iQube) adoption, premium motorcycle portfolio (Apache/Norton), and increasing market share in scooters are driving volume and profitability growth. Robust export growth across Africa, Latin America, and Asia, supported by ongoing capacity expansion and a diversified product portfolio. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 53.42, 52-week high: ₹ 4,484.50, volume: ₹ 559.91 crore 
 Technical analysis: Reclaimed its 50-DMA 
 Risk factors: Intense competition in the two-wheeler and EV segments could pressure market share, pricing power, and margins. Exposure to commodity cost inflation and demand cyclicality in domestic and export markets may impact profitability. 
 Buy: ₹ 4,198–4,261 
 Target price: ₹ 4,850 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 3950 
 Buy: Omnitech Engineering Ltd (current price: ₹ 719) 
 Why it’s recommended: Large order book from oil & gas, energy, and industrial customers provides strong revenue visibility and execution-led growth. Capacity expansion, diversification into motion control/automation and aerospace-defence opportunities can accelerate scale and margins. 
 Key metrics: P/E: NA, 52-week high: ₹ 764.85, volume: ₹ 120.37 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Delays in ramping up new facilities or executing the sizeable order book could affect growth expectations and returns. Dependence on energy-sector demand and fluctuations in raw material costs can create earnings and margin volatility. 
 Buy at: ₹ 712–723 
 Target price: ₹ 850 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 677 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Indian equity markets ended Wednesday lower, with the Nifty 50 falling 50.90 points, or 0.22%, to 22,698.85 amid sectoral weakness and selective buying. The index swung between an intraday low of 22,497.70 and a high of 22,778.05 before settling below its previous close of 22,749.75.
 Sectoral performance was mixed. Nifty Auto (+1.45%), Consumer Durables (+1.41%), Media (+1.38%), Healthcare (+1.15%) and Pharma (+1.04%) led the gains, while Oil & Gas (-2.27%) and IT (-1.98%) were the biggest laggards, followed by Realty (-0.89%) and FMCG (-0.56%). Broader market breadth remained positive, with 1,931 stocks advancing, 1,628 declining and 119 unchanged, taking the advance-decline ratio to 1.19:1.
 Technical outlook 
 The Nifty formed a small-bodied candle with a long lower shadow, signalling buying interest at lower levels. Although the index remains below key medium- and long-term moving averages, with its descending trendline intact, recent price action points to an attempt at short-term consolidation following the sharp correction.
 Momentum indicators show some improvement. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stood at 44.90, above its signal average of 43.09 but below the neutral 50 mark. The MACD was at -139.71, above its signal line of -185.41, with a positive histogram of 45.71, suggesting strengthening bullish momentum despite both readings remaining in negative territory.
 Key levels to watch 
 The 22,500–22,400 range remains a crucial support zone. A decisive break below it could trigger fresh selling, dragging the index towards 22,200–22,000. On the upside, 23,000–23,200 is likely to act as a key resistance zone following the recent breakdown from those levels.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 Nifty Bank opened lower on Wednesday but rebounded from its intraday lows to outperform the broader market. The index opened at 53,793.25, touched a high of 54,440.25 and a low of 53,626.15 before closing at 54,267.40, up 292.50 points, or 0.54%. Buying near 53,600 helped form a bullish candle with a lower shadow, signalling demand at lower levels.
 Among heavyweight constituents, State Bank of India (+1.24%), Axis Bank (+1.19%) and HDFC Bank (+0.75%) led the gains. Bank of Baroda (-0.90%), ICICI Bank (-0.67%) and Kotak Mahindra Bank (-0.56%) were the main laggards. AU Small Finance Bank (+3.67%) and IDFC First Bank (+3.04%) topped the gainers, while Yes Bank (-1.82%) was the weakest performer.
 Technical outlook 
 The 14-period Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 39.53, below its average of 43.49. Although it has recovered from around 37, it remains below the neutral 50 mark, indicating weak momentum. The MACD is at -433.10, below its signal line at -380.07, with a histogram reading of -53.03. Both lines remain in negative territory, keeping the bearish crossover intact, though the relatively narrow histogram suggests selling pressure is easing.
 The index continues to trade below its key simple moving averages (SMAs), with the 50-day SMA at 56,052 falling below the 100-day SMA

docs.title: Co-payment: The illusion of cost control
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Co-payment: The illusion of cost control
 M. S. Sahoo 4 min read 29 Oct 2026, 06:01 AM IST 
 Summary
 The co-payment proposal raises concerns about all three sources of market failure: information asymmetry, market power, and externalities. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The General Insurance Council has proposed a mandatory 10% co-payment for retail health insurance policies. The insured would bear 10% of the admissible healthcare expenses, and the insurer the remaining 90%. The proposal’s details are not yet in the public domain.
 The apparent rationale is to give the insured ‘skin in the game’. Sharing expenses may discourage unnecessary tests, procedures, prolonged hospitalization and expensive rooms, reducing insurers’ outgoings and potentially premiums.
 Health insurance accounted for 43% of the general insurance market in April-September 2026. Excluding government-sponsored schemes, the data distinguish group insurance, individual family floater, and other individual policies. Between 2018-19 and 2024-25, the average premium per person under group insurance fell 25%, from ₹ 2,975 to ₹ 2,233, while the coverage quadrupled, from 73 million to 275 million. For individual policies other than family floaters, the average premium surged 140%, from ₹ 4,662 to ₹ 11,188, while coverage fell from 15.5 million to 10.5 million.
 These trends do not establish causation, but are consistent with the proposition that, ceteris paribus, higher prices deter demand. Against this backdrop, the proposal raises concerns about three sources of market failure: information asymmetry, market power, and externalities.
 Information asymmetry
 Individuals generally know more about their health risks than insurers do. Those anticipating higher medical expenses may be more inclined to seek insurance. If healthier people leave the risk pool, average claims may rise, prompting insurers to increase premiums. Higher premiums may then drive more healthy people out of the market, further worsening the risk pool. This can trigger a vicious cycle of rising prices, adverse selection, and declining coverage.
 In 2024-25, the average premium for individual policies, other than family floaters, was about five times that for group insurance. Adding a mandatory 10% co-payment to these relatively high premiums may prompt relatively healthier individuals to exit. The resulting deterioration in the risk pool could reinforce adverse selection and further deepen exclusion.
 Market power
 Health insurance products compete on premiums, coverage, exclusions, co-payments, deductibles, hospital networks, and policy limits. A higher-premium policy with no co-payment can be as legitimate as a lower-premium policy with one. Consumers choose the balance between price and the financial protection they need.
 A uniform mandate would eliminate co-payment as a dimension of product differentiation, constrain consumer choice and potentially weaken competition. There is a material distinction between insurers independently offering co-payment as a product feature and an industry-wide proposal to impose the same requirement. The latter raises questions about collective industry influence and the preservation of competition.
 Externalities
 The proposal assumes that cost-sharing will discourage unnecessary healthcare consumption. But excessive expenditure does not always originate with patients. They often lack the medical knowledge or bargaining power to challenge hospitals’ decisions or bills. Overcharging, billing for services not rendered, duplicate claims, and unnecessary procedures are well-recognized problems in the healthcare system.
 When hospitals drive up costs that patients cannot effectively monitor or contest, co-payments can shift part of the burden to patients without correcting the underlying incentives. Patients may thus bear costs arising from failures they cannot control. Better hospital oversight, transparent pricing, rigorous claims scrutiny, and action against fraudulent billing would address these problems more directly.
 Further scrutiny needed 
 The incurred claims ratios (claims incurred divided by net earned premium) for 2024-25 were 92% for group insurance, 79% for family floaters, and 75% for other individual policies. These figures do not establish overutilization or show whether co-payment would work. They do, however, reinforce the need for evidence: if excessive utilization is the concern, it may not be the driver of only retail claims.
 Other cost drivers deserve scrutiny. Between 2023 and 2025, health premiums grew by 53%, while broker commissions grew by 118%, with retail health average commission rates increasing from 10% to 30%. This calls for examining distribution costs and incentives, alongside hospital bills. A co-payment neither reduces commissions nor prevents inflated billing. It shifts part of the cost to retail policyholders, who have weak bargaining power.
 Health insurance does not cover every healthcare expense. Outpatient treatment may be excluded, pre-existing diseases may be subject to waiting periods, and expenses beyond sub-limits or the sum insured are borne by policyholders. They may also have to bear the cost of non-admissible items. A mandatory 10% co-payment would add to this burden. It risks making healthcare and health insurance less affordable, particularly for individuals who already pay substantially higher premiums than group policyholders.
 Co-payment can be a legitimate feature of an insurance product, but consumer choice must be preserved, with appropriate safeguards for emergency treatment and affordable policies up to a specified sum insured. It should complement, not substitute for, action on hospital pricing and billing, claims scrutiny, and distribution costs. Cost-sharing must reduce costs, not merely shift the bill to policyholders.

docs.title: India’s tax department needs an AI rulebook
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 India’s tax department needs an AI rulebook
 Gautam Nayak 4 min read 28 Oct 2026, 01:24 PM IST 
 Summary
 AI is helping India’s tax department flag evasion, but its use in assessments and appeals raises concerns over privacy, accountability and human judgement. The CBDT needs a clear, transparent policy. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The Income Tax Department has officially started using artificial intelligence (AI) for various purposes. Under Project Insight and the Income Tax Transaction Analysis Centre, AI and big-data tools analyse large datasets from banks, property registrars, stock exchanges and financial institutions to build a 360-degree taxpayer profile and identify possible tax evasion and hidden assets.
 Data-driven scrutiny
 For data integration and analysis, information from the GST Network (GSTN), Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), real estate regulatory authorities (RERA), transport authorities and the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) is cross-referenced to detect mismatches between reported income and actual financial or business activity.
 Machine-learning algorithms are also used to identify cases for risk-based scrutiny. They scan tax returns, the Annual Information Statement (AIS), Tax Information Statement and Annual Tax Statement for anomalies, helping select high-risk profiles for scrutiny. In faceless assessments, scrutiny cases are allocated, notices generated and draft orders processed through automated, system-driven workflows.
 Predictive analytics, large language models ( LLMs ) and automated communications are also used to generate compliance alerts and nudges for non-filers or under-reporters. Taxpayers’ digital footprints, including high-value transactions, digital wallets and broader financial behaviour, are analysed to track potentially unreported wealth, foreign assets and virtual digital assets such as cryptocurrencies.
 The impact of these tools is evident from the fact that, during the current year, scrutiny notices have become more focused and direct in addressing relevant risk points than in earlier years. The use of AI by the tax administration has undoubtedly helped detect tax evasion and improve taxpayer compliance.
 In recent months, however, one has also noticed certain tax officials using AI for other purposes. Replies to notices are sometimes scrutinised using AI to generate subsequent notices. Some orders, including assessment orders and appeals decided by Commissioners of Income Tax (Appeals), appear to have been drafted using AI.
 This raises concerns about the accuracy of AI-generated content. In one order, reliance was placed on a Tribunal ruling to dismiss an appeal, even though the Tribunal had decided the case in precisely the opposite manner to that stated as the basis for dismissal.
 Who is accountable? 
 Several important questions arise about the use of AI for these purposes. Is such usage authorized by the tax department? How are privacy and confidentiality protected when officers use AI in these cases? What controls do senior authorities exercise over their juniors’ use of AI? Can decision-making powers and judicial discretion vested in tax authorities be delegated to AI? What recourse does a taxpayer have if an officer uses AI without authorization, or uses it incorrectly while processing an assessment or appeal?
 The Central Board of Direct Taxes ( CBDT ) needs to formulate a policy governing the use of AI by the tax department. This policy should be made public and incorporated into tax law. AI use should be transparent wherever it affects taxpayer interactions, particularly assessments and appeals, and appropriate safeguards must be built in.
 Taxpayers need to know when AI use is permissible and when it is not. There must also be an effective remedy when unauthorized use of AI by tax officials prejudices a taxpayer, including a formal reporting or grievance-redressal mechanism.
 The CBDT must also educate its officers that AI is, at best, a tool to support decision-making. It is not a substitute for, and cannot replace, the judicial decision-making of tax officers.
 Tax officers build their knowledge and experience over years through the continuous application of their minds to different cases. If they abdicate this responsibility to AI, the long-term consequence could be a generation of officers without the knowledge and judgement required to discharge their duties, potentially spelling disaster for the tax department.
 Lessons from abroad 
 Several jurisdictions, including the European Union, the UK, Australia and Singapore, have introduced policies governing AI use, supported by legal frameworks. The OECD has also published a policy paper emphasising that AI systems should be transparent, reliable, secure and subject to meaningful human oversight. It calls for accountability for AI-assisted decisions and governance mechanisms capable of identifying and correcting algorithmic errors or unintended bias.
 The underlying principle is clear: AI should support decisions, not replace human judgement.
 Given the swift and common usage of AI, it is imperative that the government and the CBDT introduce a clear and transparent policy at the earliest. Such a framework is necessary to protect taxpayers’ interests, privacy and confidentiality before affected taxpayers are forced to seek legal recourse through the courts.
 Gautam Nayak is a partner at CNK & Associates LLP. Views are personal.
