 Three things are essential for success in the stock market: knowledge, courage, and patience. Of these, knowledge is most important. One must understand there is limited capital, a limited amount of time, and a limited investment horizon. One needs to figure out how to make the best possible use of those resources to generate returns. For that, one should invest in shares that one believes have the potential to grow. That is the role of knowledge.
 The second, equally important factor is courage.
 Suppose you have ₹100, but you are always afraid. Even if you have complete conviction in a company, you might invest just ₹1 in its shares. Imagine that this particular share multiplies in value, while your other shares do not. Your overall portfolio will not generate the returns you expected because you did not invest enough in the opportunity you believed in.
 That is why courage is important.
 However, courage is a double-edged sword. It can also cause losses. Therefore, it must be backed by proper knowledge and conviction.
 And without patience, nothing works.
 We think things will turn out one way or another, but they often do not because the market is driven by two types of factors: internal and external. Internal factors include things you can study. But external factors can disrupt everything. That is why patience is essential.
 One can borrow knowledge from others, learn from other people's experience and use their knowledge to make investment decisions. One can also develop courage, but patience is something that comes from within.
 How should one approach investing? If you invest in a particular stock but get it wrong, or you buy it at the wrong time, do you stay invested? 
 There is no single theory that works for everyone. For example, one medicine might relieve my headache, while another medicine might work for you. There are different treatments for different people. The important thing is to find out what suits you.
 I do not invest with a target of 30–40 per cent. But that does not mean my approach is necessarily right and yours is wrong. In this business, one have to test themselves. If one follows someone else's formula, and it makes you uncomfortable, then perhaps that strategy is not right for them.
 That said, we must keep our minds open and learn from everyone. If someone else has progressed further than you, ask yourself what they did differently and what approach they followed.
 Can someone become a successful investor without experiencing losses, going through the struggle, and facing difficult periods? 
 Nobody can become a successful investor without experiencing a loss. It is impossible to go through the market without suffering losses, experiencing anxiety, feeling worried, or facing difficult situations and still expect to become successful.
 One must use these experiences as sources of knowledge, and not consider them enemies. The real test for an investor is how you behave during a bear market. One needs to reflect on themselves and their portfolio. If you understand the lessons that losses offer, you can grow as an investor.
 Has losing money changed the way you look at risk and how you deal with it as an investor? 
 Earlier, my financial resources were limited, and they are still limited today, although the scale has changed somewhat. When you have limited money, you naturally feel concerned about losing it.
 But making money in the stock market and creating wealth are two different things. The stock market is fundamentally a game of risk, and you create wealth by taking risks.

India not yet a consensus buy amid oil, tech disruptions: Global brokerages
 India is yet to emerge as a consensus buy for foreign investors, with relative growth prospects, elevated oil prices and uncertain IT earnings weighing on inflows.
 India not yet a consensus buy amid oil, tech disruptions: Global brokerages
 Puneet Wadhwa Heena Ojha New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 28 2026 | 8:40 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 While India remains a structurally attractive emerging market (EM), global investors are no longer seeing it as an obvious buy. Slower relative growth, elevated oil prices, uncertain earnings visibility, and technology-led disruption are weighing on foreign investment flows, stressed panellists at the Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit 2026 in Mumbai.
 Sandeep Bhatia, managing director and head of equity India at Macquarie Capital, said that India’s position in the emerging market pecking order has weakened in terms of investor flows during a session on 'Analysing markets through the global lens', moderated by Puneet Wadhwa.
 He said these flows did not necessarily change India’s structural position permanently, pointing to developments in other emerging markets, including Indonesia, China and Brazil. However, a correction in the technology-led rally in Western markets could prompt global investors to reassess India.
 “When this entire AI tech-driven euphoria, which is happening in the Western markets, sees a correction, there would definitely be a re-evaluation of the Indian market,” he said.
 The relative attractiveness of Indian equities has diminished as growth and earnings prospects in developed markets strengthened, according to Gautam Chhaochharia, head of global markets, India, at UBS. He said sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows would require an improvement in India’s relative growth outlook and a reduction in macroeconomic risks.

 Globally, investors are also increasingly comparing India’s investment opportunities with technology-led developments in other markets, raising questions about the appeal of Indian large-cap companies focused on traditional businesses.
 Venugopal Garre, managing director at Bernstein, said the challenge extends beyond artificial intelligence (AI), as technology is increasingly capable of disrupting businesses across sectors. “The reality is that technology disruption, which is essentially happening, is not just isolated to AI as a technology. It’s about AI as a technology going to disrupt a lot of things in every sector,” he said.
 According to Garre, global investors are looking for businesses with the potential to become future multibaggers, develop export opportunities and benefit from emerging technologies. Traditional businesses, he said, needed to demonstrate sufficiently strong growth to compete for that capital.
 “My problem simply today is that foreign investors, when they look at opportunities, they will say, ‘What is the point of investing in a traditional, old-school end market unless there is massive growth which forces me to invest? Let me look for opportunities which can be future multi-baggers, big stories, export stories,” Garre said.
 He also said that Indian large-cap companies needed to take greater responsibility for investing in future technologies rather than waiting for government policy support.
 Chhaochharia said the outlook for Indian IT services companies remained uncertain from an investor’s perspective, despite the opportunities created by the adoption of AI. He said investors were looking beyond the immediate earnings outlook and assessing whether the sector could return to sustained double-digit earnings growth over the next three to five years.
 “Indian IT services is still evolving in the AI world. There is an opportunity as global businesses implement AI, which is a complex task,” Chhaochharia said. However, he said investors did not yet have sufficient visibility on a sustained recovery in earnings growth.
 IT index valuations have declined, but are not sufficiently attractive relative to global IT services companies or the broader Indian market.
 On India Inc’s earnings outlook beyond IT, Chhaochharia was more optimistic. He said nominal gross domestic product growth, despite the headwinds facing the economy, remained around double digits, making double-digit corporate earnings growth a reasonable expectation.
 He said the more important question for investors was whether earnings growth could reach 18-20 per cent, rather than 10-14 per cent, which he said should be reasonably achievable over the longer term.
 Market drivers 
 Apart from earnings growth, lower oil prices, reduced pressure on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) from capital outflows and some moderation in developed-market growth are factors that could improve India’s relative attractiveness, according to Chhaochharia.
 Oil, according to him, is more important than US Treasury yields as a near-term driver of sentiment and foreign investment flows into India, although US rates remained important for longer-term investors. Higher US interest rates had raised the return threshold Indian equities need to meet in dollar terms.
 Sanjay Mookim, head of India equity research at JP Morgan, also highlighted the impact of higher crude prices on India’s external balances and currency.
 He said every $10 increase in crude oil prices, sustained over a year, increased India’s current account deficit by about $15 billion.

 Stock Market LIVE: GIFT Nifty down 56 points; Asia markets turn mixed; Brent crude trades at $114
 SI Reporter New Delhi 
 Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates, Thursday, Oct 29, 2026: T he GIFT Nifty indicated that the Nifty 50 will open lower; the futures were quoted at 22,685, down 0.21 per cent.
 Asian markets were trading mixed despite a slight cool-off in oil prices amid tensions in West Asia. Japan’s Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi were trading 0.15 per cent higher and 2.28 per cent lower, respectively.
 Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 ended 0.19 per cent and 0.28 per cent up, respectively. The Nasdaq Composite settled 0.27 per cent up.
 Crude oil prices inched marginally lower as they slipped below $115 per barrel. The July future contract was quoted at $114.9, down 0.36 per cent.
 Gold futures were down 0.27 per cent and silver futures were trading 0.42 per cent down.
 Q2 results

 Bombay Coated & Special Steels Ltd. IPO opens today, October 29, 2026. Meanwhile, SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd. and BLS Polymers Ltd. IPOs will close today.

docs.title: Jio Platforms: Nomura initiates ‘Buy’ with 20% upside target on impending tariff hikes
docs.text: India’s telecom sector has grown into the world’s second largest subscriber base in a span of around 30 years. As Jio Platforms debuts on exchanges today, October 28, Japanese brokerage Nomura has initiated coverage on Jio Platforms, with a target price of Rs 1,340. This implies an upside of nearly 20% from its issue price of Rs 1,119 apiece. Nomura said Jio’s focus has shifted from adding users to earning more from each customer. Three tariff hikes since 2019 have nearly doubled the company’s mobile broadband average revenue per user (ARPU) to Rs 200 in FY26, yet data costs only Rs 7.5 per GB. This is much lower when compared with Rs 33 in China and Rs 228 in the US. The brokerage expects India’s mobile market grow to Rs 5.2 lakh crore by FY31 from Rs 2.9 lakh crore in FY26. Jio, which was once the disruptor, is now the leader, with around 42% of the nation’s wireless subscribers, 60% of data traffic, and 43% of home broadband. Nomura expects Jio Platforms to report a healthy earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) growth of 13.5% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY26 to FY29. ALSO READThe ‘anti-China’ EV battery trade: 2 Indian chemical stocks taking on China’s dominance Here’s what is driving the Japanese brokerage’s rationale - Nomura on Jio Platforms: Price hikes to follow exchange debut Nomura believes the listing of Jio Platforms is likely to push the company, which is the price setter, towards steady tariff hikes that its peers can follow. It expects industrywide tariff hikes of 15% in Nov-Dec this year, as the last hike was in July 2024. “We think that Jio deliberately held back the hike ahead of its IPO to protect subscriber momentum which got impacted in the last tariff hike. With the listing done, the incentive now shifts firmly toward earnings growth,” Nomura said. Every Rs 10 increase in ARPU drives a meaningful growth in EBITDA . “.though Jio's transmission ratio of ~49% over the next 3 quarters (as per previous tariff hike cycle) is lower than Airtel's ~69% due to more number of subscribers on long-duration prepaid plans, in our view,” it added. Nomura on Jio Platforms: Long-term value creation Jio Platforms is the largest telecom operator in India with around 41.7% wireless subscriber market share. With its largest 5G coverage, the highest data usage per subscriber, around 27% higher than Airtel, and lowest churn among peers, Nomura believes Jio is “well placed” to leverage its strength to reduce its ARPU gap with Airtel. “The 15% industrywide tariff hike in Nov–Dec 2026 could be an immediate trigger for higher ARPU, while in the medium-to-long term, Jio will likely lean towards tariff repair via a shift from flat unlimited data bundles to tiered pricing, and/or premiumisation via network slicing on 5G,” Nomura said. Nomura on Jio Platforms: Home broadband as the second growth engine The company’s fixed broadband base reached 2.86 crore subscribers by June 2026, against 1.47 crore for Airtel, largely due to its increasingly aggressive fixed wireless access-based rollout strategy. India's home broadband penetration currently stands at just 21%, compared to a global average of over 70%, pointing to an addressable base of over 30 crore households and a decade-long growth runway. ALSO READJio Platforms IPO Listing Live Updates: Big debut or a surprise? Check GMP, share price “We believe Jio's FWA model is capital-efficient, as it leases CPE equipment from third-party lessees, unlike FTTH, where ~25% of home passes don't get converted and the fiber cost is sunk,” the brokerage said. Nomura on Jio Platforms: Downside risks The Japanese brokerage said any delays in tariff hikes or lower-than-expects tariff increases are downside risks to its forecast. Nomura also said costlier handsets and equipment are also some of the other downside risks. Jio Platforms: Well placed for firm growth Nomura expects the company’s listing to open the way for industry-wide tariff hikes, which is also likely to bridge its ARPU gap with Airtel. Home broadband connections are seen as the second levers of growth, according to Nomura. docs.title: Is Vodafone Idea a Buy now? Jefferies outlines 3 scenarios with up to 143% upside
docs.text: Can a stock that has fallen 23% still hold a big surprise? Global investment bank Jefferies has kept a ‘Buy’ rating on Vodafone Idea (Vi). However, it has cut its target price to Rs 16 from Rs 20. That still means a 34% rise from the current market price. The eye-catcher, though, is an upside scenario that points to 143% gain potential from current levels. Its upside scenario analysis also presents a more optimistic price target of Rs 29 while the downside scenario projects possibility of the price falling to Rs 9. What could determine which direction the stock takes? Vodafone Idea: Jefferies outlines 3 scenarios, 3 possible outcomes The brokerage has mapped three possible paths. According to the Jefferies report, Vodafone Idea’s valuation depends heavily on how much telecom tariffs rise over the next few years and how quickly the company can improve its earnings. ScenarioTarget pricePotential returnBase caseRs 1634%Upside caseRs 29143%Downside caseRs 9-25% In its base case, Jefferies assumes a single 15% tariff hike in April 2027. It expects revenue and cash EBITDA to grow at compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 11% and 25%, respectively, between FY26-29. ALSO READElon Musk’s Starlink is at India’s Door. 4 Sectors That Could Feel it First The upside case assumes cumulative tariff hikes of 25% between FY27-29. Under this scenario, the brokerage values the stock at Rs 29, implying a potential gain of 143%. But if tariffs remain unchanged over the same period, its downside scenario places the target at Rs 9, indicating a possible fall of 25%. Vodafone Idea: Why has Jefferies retained its 'Buy' rating? Vodafone Idea’s share price has corrected 23% from its September levels. According to Jefferies report, the outlook for its FY2028 EBITDA remains unchanged in consensus estimates. The improvement in subscriber trends is an important part of the investment case. The Jefferies report noted that the network expansion has helped stabilise subscriber trends. The company increased its broadband base stations by 39% and network sites by 14% over the past two years. Jefferies expects Vodafone Idea’s network sites to increase by 26% to 2,61,000 by FY29. Tariff hikes could make a significant difference Higher mobile tariffs are central to Jefferies’ optimistic outlook. The report noted, “Given VIL's high operating leverage (~20% cash EBITDA margins), we estimate every 10% tariff hike drives a 17% increase in its cash EBITDA.” It also noted that Vodafone Idea’s enterprise value-to-market capitalisation ratio is 2.2 times. Is Vodafone Idea cheap compared with its past valuations? Valuation is another factor behind the brokerage’s call. The telecom player, Vodafone Idea is trading at around 21 times its enterprise value to cash EBITDA, below its five-year average, according to Jefferies. The brokerage believes the valuation could remain elevated until earnings growth strengthens and cash EBITDA margins improve to above 40%. It expects these levels to be achievable around FY32-33. Jefferies also estimates that the company could deliver an annualised return of 16% through March 2032, assuming a 12-times valuation multiple on its FY2033 cash EBITDA. This is a longer-term estimate, not a guaranteed return. ALSO READVi allows pan-India data sharing in new prepaid family plan What investors need to watch The biggest uncertainty is whether the company can implement tariff increases while keeping subscribers. Jefferies added “VI's fair value ranges between Rs 9-29/share, implying 143% upside potential and 25% downside potential”. The report noted, “We lower our target multiple to 20x EV/EBITDA due to higher yields and reiterate 'Buy' with lowered price target of Rs 16” Disclaimer: This article is based on research reports from one or more brokerage firms and is for informational purposes only. docs.title: Tata Capital to Paytm: Ambit Capital names 6 stocks with 13% to 59% upside
docs.text: Ambit Capital has retained 'Buy' ratings on six stocks across financial services, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, digital payments and industrial equipment, with target prices indicating potential upside of up to 59%. Kirloskar Pneumatic, Tata Capital and SBI Life Insurance offer the highest implied upside among the stocks covered, while Paytm, Acutaas Chemicals and Cipla also feature on the brokerage's list. The recommendations follow a mixed set of second-quarter results. Some companies reported stronger operating performance or improving business prospects, while others faced execution delays, slower growth or pressure on profitability. Ambit's calls hinge on company-specific triggers, including a recovery in industrial equipment dispatches, accelerating loan growth, insurance margin expansion, operating leverage in digital payments and new product opportunities in chemicals and pharmaceuticals. Ambit on Kirloskar Pneumatic: 'Buy' Kirloskar Pneumatic offers the highest implied upside in Ambit Capital's selection, with a target price of Rs 850 indicating an upside of around 59%. The brokerage retained its 'Buy' rating despite cutting its target price from Rs 965 and lowering earnings estimates for FY27 to FY29 by 8% to 11%. The reduction followed a weak second quarter, when revenue fell 15.6% year-on-year to Rs 3.26 billion and EBITDA declined 30.4% to Rs 407 million. EBITDA margin contracted 260 basis points to 12.5%, as delayed precision engineering dispatches and Middle East shipment deferrals hurt execution and operating leverage. ALSO READL&T to BEL, HAL: 12 defence stocks in focus after DAC clears Rs 2.12 lk cr procurement Order inflows, however, increased 56.3% year-on-year to Rs 5.13 billion, beating Ambit's estimate by 14.1%. The order backlog rose 22.4% year-on-year to Rs 20.4 billion. Demand for refrigeration equipment, renewed activity in CNG compressors and growth in niche gas compressor applications supported the order outlook. Ambit expects the resumption of delayed precision engineering dispatches in the second half of FY27 to support revenue recovery. The company is also developing opportunities in defence and precision industrial applications, while the ramp-up of its Zephyros product line could contribute to growth in FY28 and FY29. The brokerage said, "We remain constructive on KKPC’s transition towards a technology-led solutions business, despite a weak 1HFY27 due to the Middle East-related shipment delays and PED dispatch deferments, which have resulted in negative operating leverage." The key test is whether the company can convert its order backlog into revenue without further delays. Management retained its FY27 target of double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margins of 18% to 20%, although Ambit cautioned that these targets appeared challenging after the first-half performance. Ambit on Tata Capital: 'Buy' Tata Capital is a preferred pick for Ambit, which set a target price of Rs 463. The target implies upside of 54.3%. The brokerage's positive view rests on accelerating assets under management growth, improving asset quality and rising return on equity. AUM growth accelerated to 26.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27, compared with 22% in the first quarter. Wholesale loans grew 58%, while small and medium enterprise loans increased 38%. Growth in unsecured personal and business loans also accelerated to 20%, from 13% in the previous quarter. Asset quality improved, with estimated net slippages declining around 30% year-on-year and credit costs falling to 0.9% from 1.3%. Return on equity reached 14% in the quarter, continuing the improvement seen since the company's listing. Ambit expects Tata Capital to benefit from the growth in higher-margin lending products, a broad distribution network and its ability to compete on funding costs. The brokerage also sees potential support from lending rate increases, given the company's greater share of floating-rate assets relative to liabilities. Ambit said, "Recent stock price correction is unwarranted given AUM growth acceleration, RoE expansion and rate-hike cycle benefits." It projected AUM and earnings per share to grow at compound annual growth rates of 21% and 31%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29. Risks include higher funding costs, competitive pressure on lending yields and uncertainty around growth in motor finance. Ambit on SBI Life Insurance: 'Buy' Ambit retained its 'Buy' rating on SBI Life Insurance with a target price of Rs 2,350, implying upside of around 43.9%. The insurer's individual annualised premium equivalent grew 9.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27, but a 10.8% decline in group APE limited overall APE growth to 7.1%. Despite the moderate growth, profitability improved as value of new business increased 12% year-on-year and the VNB margin expanded 130 basis points to 29.2%. The company benefited from a more favourable product mix, including contributions from non-participating savings and annuity products. Its solvency ratio stood at 1.97 times, while embedded value increased 14.9% year-on-year to Rs 873.5 billion. Ambit retained its estimates, building in 14% APE growth between FY26 and FY29 and an average VNB margin of around 27.2%. Management reiterated its FY27 guidance of 14% to 15% individual APE growth and a VNB margin of 26% to 28%. The brokerage said, "We remain positive on SBI Life given its unparalleled distribution (owing to SBI) and brand name." docs.title: Jio Platforms: Elara initiates coverage, sees valuation at Rs 12.58 lakh crore by FY29
docs.text: Elara Securities initiated coverage on Jio Platforms with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,367, citing the company’s potential to increase average revenue per user (ARPU), expand its home broadband business and grow revenue from digital products and services. The brokerage expected Jio Platforms to report a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13% in revenue, 16% in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), and 23% in profit after tax (PAT) between FY26 and FY29. Elara valued the company at 11.5 times its estimated FY29 EBITDA to arrive at the target price. It estimated that ARPU would increase at a CAGR of around 6% between FY26 and FY29, with higher ARPU contributing about two-thirds of incremental revenue over the period. ALSO READRs 1,000 cr AI deal, 334.8% profit growth: 2 stocks riding India’s GPU boom The brokerage also identified digital products and services as a key growth driver. It projected revenue from this business to rise at a CAGR of around 23% and EBITDA at around 36% during FY26-FY29. Elara said, “We expect a top-line CAGR of 13%, an EBITDA CAGR of 16%, and a PAT CAGR of 23% during FY26-FY29.” The company’s large subscriber base and technology infrastructure could help it generate additional revenue from services beyond mobile connectivity. These include cloud services, artificial intelligence, enterprise solutions, cybersecurity, entertainment and connected-home offerings. Tariff increases could support Jio Platforms’ profitability Elara expected telecom tariff increases to contribute to higher ARPU and earnings. It also pointed to the need for operators to earn returns on their investments in 5G networks as a factor supporting tariff rationalisation. The brokerage estimated Jio’s ARPU at Rs 214 for FY26 and projected it to increase to Rs 229 in FY27, Rs 245 in FY28 and Rs 257 in FY29. However, Jio’s ARPU was expected to remain below that of Bharti Airtel. Elara estimated Bharti Airtel’s ARPU at Rs 257 in FY26, rising to Rs 315 by FY29, compared with Jio’s projected Rs 257. ALSO READHAL to BEL: Goldman Sachs names 10 beneficiaries of Rs 2.12 lk cr defence procurement plan Elara also noted that the timing of tariff increases could affect the pace of revenue growth. It said its estimates allowed for a relatively modest initial increase, partly because Jio Prime membership pricing was locked until September 2027, potentially deferring some benefits to FY28. JioAirFiber and home broadband offer another growth avenue Elara identified home broadband as another major opportunity for Jio Platforms, supported by JioFiber and JioAirFiber. Fixed wireless access allows the company to extend broadband services to locations where laying fibre to individual homes may be difficult. According to the report, Jio had 28.6 million fixed broadband subscribers in the first quarter of FY27, giving it around 43.3% of India’s fixed broadband market. The brokerage estimated that its home broadband subscriber base could increase from 27 million in FY26 to 66 million by FY29. The report stated, “JPL is India's largest fixed broadband provider, with 29 million customers in Q1FY27 at 43% market share, nearly 1.9x BHARTI's subscriber base (Source: company).” Elara also noted Jio’s strong position in fixed wireless access. Its estimates indicated that Jio held around 78.7% of the 5G and unlicensed band radio-based fixed wireless access market in the first quarter of FY27. The brokerage expected rising broadband affordability and demand for home connectivity to support further subscriber additions. Digital products and enterprise services could improve earnings mix Beyond its core telecom operations, Jio Platforms offers consumer and enterprise services spanning cloud infrastructure, the Internet of Things, cybersecurity, entertainment and managed digital solutions. Elara expected these businesses to grow faster than the core connectivity business. Its projections called for digital products and services EBITDA to rise at a CAGR of around 36% between FY26 and FY29. Enterprise services could benefit from increasing demand for cloud adoption, connected devices, managed networks and digital transformation. Jio’s existing network and customer relationships could also help it distribute additional services. The brokerage also discussed the potential for 5G network slicing, which allows operators to provide dedicated network capacity with different performance levels. However, it said the technology remained at an early stage of commercial adoption and had not factored any meaningful contribution from it into its FY26-FY29 estimates. EBITDA margins expected to expand by FY29 Elara projected Jio Platforms’ consolidated EBITDA margin to rise from around 50% in FY26 to 53.8% in FY29, an expansion of about 387 basis points. The brokerage expected revenue growth, higher ARPU and increased contributions from digital products and services to support earnings. It also forecast a 23% CAGR in PAT during FY26-FY29. Its valuation was based on estimated FY29 EBITDA of around Rs 1.13 lakh crore and a target multiple of 11.5 times. After accounting for estimated net debt, Elara arrived at an equity value of approximately Rs 12.58 lakh crore and a target price of Rs 1,367 per share. docs.title: Jio Platforms surges 21% on debut: Is a 15% tariff hike next? What Motilal Oswal forecasts
docs.text: Check your phone. Chances are, you are one of the 53.3 crore people who pay Jio every month. That is why today’s listing matters. Jio Platform (JPL) debuted as India’s largest initial public offering (IPO), at a 21% premium to the upper end of its price range. Motilal Oswal has initiated coverage on the stock with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,350, implying an upside of around 21% from the issue price. The report calls the company “The gateway of digital India!” Before Jio arrived, India had more than 12 telecom companies. According to Motilal Oswal report, Jio’s entry forced the sector to consolidate into what it calls a “3+1” market structure. Now the key question is – will your bill go up? Motilal Oswal’s report assumes a tariff hike of about 15% in March 2027. Let’s see what else it says. Jio’s next growth driver: Will higher tariffs lift earnings? One of the key factors that could influence Jio’s financial performance is how much it earns from each wireless subscriber. According to Motilal Oswal report, Jio Platforms could benefit from a possible 15% smartphone tariff hike in March 2027. The brokerage expects higher tariffs, along with new subscriber additions, to support revenue growth. It expects Jio Platforms’ consolidated revenue, reported earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), and profit after tax (PAT) to grow at compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 14%, 15% and 20%, respectively, between FY26-29. ALSO READJio Platforms IPO Listing Live Updates: Jio lists at 21% premium, becomes India’s largest telco with Rs 12.5 lakh crore market cap The report noted, “We expect RJio to deliver a CAGR of ~11%/13% in wireless revenue/EBITDA over FY26-29, extending its market leadership in consumer wireless subs and wireless revenue by 120bps / 100bps over FY26-FY29.” The brokerage expects Reliance Jio to increase its revenue and operating earnings while strengthening its position in the wireless market. Home broadband: Another opportunity for Jio Wireless services are not the only potential source of growth. Jio’s home broadband business, which includes fibre and AirFiber connections, could also contribute to its earnings. According to the brokerage report, India’s home broadband market still has room to expand because penetration remains low. Jio could benefit as more households seek high-speed internet connections. Motilal Oswal expects Jio to account for around 73% of incremental home broadband subscriber additions in the industry between FY26-29. It also expects the company’s home broadband subscriber base to reach around 5 crore by FY29. The report added, “We expect RJio’s HBB revenue to deliver a CAGR of ~27% over FY26-29, with its contribution rising to ~12% of RJio’s revenue by FY29 (from ~8% currently).” Can Jio become a net cash company by FY29? A major part of Jio’s outlook is its ability to generate cash after years of investment in network infrastructure. The company’s spending on capital expenditure moderated to around Rs 34,000 crore in FY26 after the completion of its pan-India fifth-generation (5G) network rollout. Motilal Oswal expects annual capital expenditure to remain between Rs 34,000 crore and Rs 36,000 crore over the medium term. According to the brokerage report, “Rising profitability and range-bound capex should generate a cumulative FCF of Rs 1.46 trillion over FY26-29 and enable JPL to achieve a net cash position by FY29.” ALSO READJio Platforms lists at 21% premium: How India’s biggest IPO fares vs 5 largest issues What is Motilal Oswal’s target price for Jio Platforms? Motilal Oswal has set a target price of Rs 1,350 per share, based on a discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation and an estimated 11.5 times FY2029 EBITDA multiple. The brokerage believes Jio could command a premium to Bharti Airtel’s India business because of its market position, potential influence on industry tariffs and limited share availability in the market. However, the outlook is not without risks. Delays in tariff hikes, stronger competition, higher capital expenditure and slower growth in digital services could affect earnings. The brokerage also cautions that changes in ARPU could materially affect its valuation estimates. It sees a bull-case target price of Rs 1,690 and a bear-case target price of Rs 1,035. docs.title: Jio Platforms finishes 27% above IPO price: Buy, sell or hold India’s most valuable telco?
docs.text: Jio, the service millions of Indians use every day to make calls, stream videos and scroll through their phones, became a listed company today. The Jio Platforms shares made their debut on the stock exchanges this morning and opened at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium over the issue price of Rs 1,119. By the end of Day 1, the stock had settled at Rs 1,419 on both the NSE and BSE. Jio Platforms: The IPO journey The journey to the trading floor began on October 21, when Jio’s initial public offer opened for investors. Bidding continued for three days and closed on October 23, also the birthday of Jio Platforms MD, Akash Ambani and his twin sister, Isha Ambani’. Allotment, the step where applicants find out whether they received shares, was finalised on October 26. Today, October 28, the shares started trading, and company officials rang the opening bell to mark the first session. Jio Platforms shares closed at Rs 1,419 on both the NSE and BSE, up 4.49%, from their listing price of Rs 1,358. Compared with the IPO issue price of Rs 1,119, the stock ended its first trading day marking a gain of 26.81%. ALSO READJio Platforms surges 21% on debut: Is a 15% tariff hike next? What Motilal Oswal forecasts Jio Platforms kicks off trade on a high note The company had sold shares at Rs 1,119 each in an issue worth Rs 30,200 crore. When trading opened on the NSE, the price jumped to Rs 1,358. The BSE showed the same opening price, which works out to a premium of 21.36%. Put simply, anyone who got shares at the issue price was sitting on a paper gain of Rs 239 per share the moment trading began. A family moment at the exchange The listing ceremony drew the Ambani family. Mukesh Ambani was there with his wife Nita Ambani, along with their children Akash, Isha and Anant. Akash is Jio’s managing director. Jio Platforms becomes largest listed telecom firm in India At its listing price, Jio Platforms has a market value of about Rs 12.5 lakh crore. That makes it one of the biggest companies in India. Two rankings changed as a result. Jio has moved ahead of Bharti Airtel to become the most valuable telecom company in the country, and its parent, Reliance Industries, is now the most valuable business group in India. ALSO READJio Platforms: Nomura initiates ‘Buy’ with 20% upside target on impending tariff hikes Jio Platforms shares: Should investors buy, sell or hold? Investors considering the stock will also need to look at its earnings outlook, the scope for tariff increases and the company's ability to generate higher revenue from its existing customer base. Motilal Oswal has initiated coverage on Jio Platforms with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,350. The brokerage's target is based on its assessment of the company's longer-term earnings potential. It expects Jio to benefit from a possible 15% smartphone tariff hike in March 2027, alongside additional subscriber growth. Higher tariffs could help the company increase revenue per user, although the timing and extent of any increase remain uncertain. Nomura has initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,340, implying around 20% upside from the IPO price of Rs 1,119. The brokerage estimates EBITDA to grow at a CAGR of about 13.5% between FY26 and FY29. Nomura noted that Jio has around 42% of India's wireless subscribers, accounts for nearly 60% of data traffic and has a 43% share of the home broadband market. It expects Jio's position in the sector to support gradual tariff increases that competitors could also follow. ALSO READJio Platforms lists at 21% premium: How India’s biggest IPO fares vs 5 largest issues Elara Securities has also initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,367. Its outlook rests on potential improvements in average revenue per user (ARPU), expansion of the home broadband business and growth in digital services. The brokerage expects Jio Platforms' revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13% between FY26 and FY29. It forecasts EBITDA growth of 16% and profit after tax growth of 23% over the same period. EBITDA measures earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, while CAGR shows the average annual growth rate over a period. docs.title: Piramal vs Syngene vs Divi’s Labs: Kotak sees up to 58% upside in select CRDMO stocks
docs.text: Indian contract research, development and manufacturing organisations (CRDMOs) are entering a period in which the capacity built over the past few years could begin translating into stronger revenue growth. Kotak Institutional Equities expects the sector to benefit from customer-backed investments, improving utilisation and rising demand for specialised manufacturing, particularly in peptides and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). In its October 26, 2026 report, Kotak said the expansion cycle had temporarily weighed on asset turnover and returns, as new facilities remained under construction, underwent validation or operated below optimal utilisation. The brokerage expects the benefits to become more visible over FY27-30 as additional molecules reach commercial production. Kotak named Piramal Pharma and Sai Life Sciences as its preferred stocks in the sector. It maintained a 'Buy' rating on Piramal Pharma and an 'Add' rating on Sai Life Sciences, while retaining a 'Buy' rating on Syngene International. It maintained 'Sell' ratings on Divi’s Laboratories and Laurus Labs, citing elevated valuations despite improving business prospects. Kotak’s estimates point to an important distinction between business growth and stock valuations. The brokerage sees substantial revenue potential across the sector, but believes that elevated valuations limit the investment case for Divi’s and Laurus. Piramal Pharma offers a combination of integrated capabilities and valuation headroom, while Sai provides exposure to expanding manufacturing capacity and newer technologies. ALSO READL&T to BEL, HAL: 12 defence stocks in focus after DAC clears Rs 2.12 lk cr procurement Indian CRDMOs prepare for a revenue ramp-up as new capacity comes onstream The sector’s investment cycle has gathered pace as companies expand conventional manufacturing and build capabilities in peptides, ADCs, oligonucleotides, highly potent active pharmaceutical ingredients (HPAPIs) and biologics. Kotak estimated that aggregate capital expenditure among the Indian CRDMOs covered in its analysis would rise to Rs 7,940 crore in FY27, from Rs 6,460 crore in FY26. It projected spending of Rs 5,650 crore in FY28 and Rs 5,400 crore in FY29. The brokerage believes the scale of investment is supported by customer requirements, dedicated projects, capacity reservations and long-term manufacturing arrangements. These commitments could reduce the risk that newly built facilities remain underutilised for extended periods. ALSO READThe ‘anti-China’ EV battery trade: 2 Indian chemical stocks taking on China’s dominance Kotak’s report stated, “We believe this visible outsourcing pipeline sets up FY27-30E for stronger utilization, revenue conversion and operating leverage as new capacity comes onstream.” Divi’s Laboratories, Laurus Labs, Sai Life Sciences and Piramal Pharma are among the companies making sizeable investments in manufacturing infrastructure and specialised capabilities. Blue Jet Healthcare is also expanding capacity, while Syngene International is investing in biologics, peptides and ADC-related infrastructure. The payoff will depend on how quickly customer programmes progress from development and validation to commercial manufacturing. A larger asset base does not automatically produce higher revenue, but customer-backed projects could make the utilisation ramp-up more predictable. Biotech funding remains a risk, but customer-backed projects offer protection The recent improvement in biotech funding has supported investment in outsourced drug development and manufacturing. Kotak noted that private equity and venture capital funding for biotechnology had started to recover from the second half of calendar year 2025 and remained robust in 2026. However, funding conditions are not uniformly strong across the industry. The brokerage cautioned that investment was becoming more concentrated, leaving early-stage discovery activity more exposed to any deterioration in funding. A sustained slowdown could eventually affect demand for outsourced research and manufacturing, particularly where capacity has been built without firm customer commitments. The impact may be less severe for facilities dedicated to specific customer programmes or supported by long-term arrangements. Kotak wrote, “A sustained slowdown in biotech funding can affect CDMO capex, but usually with a lag and much more strongly for speculative capacity than for committed/customer-backed projects.” The brokerage therefore expects the sector’s near-term growth visibility to remain broadly intact, even if biotech funding moderates. Its assessment rests on the proportion of current investments backed by customer demand rather than on funding conditions alone. This distinction is particularly relevant for companies expanding facilities for identified commercial programmes. It is less reassuring for businesses where new capacity still needs to attract meaningful contracts and generate sales. Peptides and ADCs emerge as key growth opportunities A defining feature of the current investment cycle is the growing emphasis on specialised manufacturing platforms. Kotak identified peptides, ADCs, oligonucleotides, HPAPIs and biologics as important opportunities as drug developers increasingly pursue complex therapies. These products often require specialised infrastructure, more stringent containment standards and greater process-development expertise than conventional small-molecule manufacturing. docs.title: Bajaj Auto share price jumps 4%: Brokerages see up to 20% upside on exports, EV expansion
docs.text: The Bajaj Auto share price jumped nearly 4% today, October 28, after its quarterly results beat the Street’s estimates. Brokerages see new product launches driving growth in the domestic market, and exports are expected to continue to do well. However, some margin pressure is likely in the near term from rising commodity costs. Bajaj Auto Q2 earnings Bajaj Auto on Tuesday reported a 35.2% year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone net profit to Rs 3,353.76 crore for Q2FY27, beating Bloomberg estimates of Rs 3,152 crore. Strong export demand and growth in its electric vehicle portfolio supported the company’s performance for the quarter. ALSO READDouble-digit profit growth, stocks down up to 43%: 4 names worth a fresh look Its revenue from operations rose 34.1% YoY to Rs 20,003.43 crore, crossing the Rs 20,000-crore mark for the first time, from Rs 14,922.05 crore a year ago. It beat Bloomberg estimates of Rs 18,918 crore. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 36.7% to Rs 4,170.83 crore from Rs 3,051.66 crore in the year-ago quarter, against estimates of Rs 3,909 crore. EBITDA margin expanded to 20.85% from 20.45% a year ago. Jefferies on Bajaj Auto: Near-term margin outlook cautious Global investment bank Jefferies retained ‘Hold’ rating on Bajaj Auto, and has a price target of Rs 11,500, implying an upside of around 10% from the current price of Rs 10,490 apiece. The company’s EBITDA margin has recovered despite severe commodity inflation. However, the management seemed a bit cautious on the margin outlook for the near term as commodity prices continue to rise and the rupee has slightly strengthened of late. Jefferies expects it to deliver an EBITDA margin of 20-21% in FY27 to FY29. Bajaj Auto plans to launch two new brands in the 125-200cc bikes in FY27. “2W demand momentum remains strong in both India and export markets. Bajaj is doing well in EVs and has regained some share in exports, although domestic motorcycle market share has been under pressure,” Jefferies said. Nomura on Bajaj Auto: New bike launches key catalyst for domestic market Nomura has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock but reduced the target price by 3% to Rs 11,855. This implies an upside of 13% from the current price. Nomura sees strong growth continuing in EVs and healthy growth in exports. The key catalyst will be the success of two new brand launches in the domestic market. Growth in the local market is expected to be led by Chetak. The brokerage has lowered its EBITDA margin forecast to 20.3% for FY27 from 21.1%, due to some more cost pressure in the near term due to high commodity prices. For FY28, it has lowered EBITDA outlook to 21.1% from 21.4% and to 20.3% for FY29 from 20.8%. Motilal Oswal on Bajaj Auto: Domestic share to recover gradually The domestic brokerage has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, with a target price of Rs 12,600. This implies an upside of 20% from the current price of Rs 10,490 apiece. ALSO READEicher to TVS Motor: Why Jefferies is betting on two-wheelers this festive season The company is expected to gradually recover market share in the domestic motorcycle market, driven by a healthy launch pipeline. Bajaj Auto’s export outlook continues to be healthy, with the management targeting over 250,000 units per month in the near term. Motilal Oswal has raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimate by 5% for FY27, on the back of a better-than-expected top line in Q2 due to higher PLI income and export incentives. The company also continues to outperform even in electric vehicles, both two-wheelers and three-wheelers. “Given the strong earnings forecast, healthy return ratios, among-the-best dividend payouts and a resilient business model, valuations at 21.8x FY27E/FY28E EPS appear attractive,” the brokerage added. However, rising commodity prices could pose some challenges in the near term. Bajaj Auto continues to outperform in EV sales as well, and plans to expand this segment. docs.title: Jio Platforms races past brokerages’ 12-month targets on debut
docs.text: Jio Platforms has taken just one trading session to race past the 12-month price targets set by some of the leading brokerages. The stock's stellar market debut on Wednesday saw it close at Rs 1,419, up nearly 27% from its issue price of Rs 1,119 and comfortably above the targets set by Nomura, Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Elara Capital. All three brokerages initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating, betting on higher average revenue per user (ARPU), tariff hikes, expansion in home broadband and new revenue streams from digital services and international technology licensing. ALSO READJio Platforms financials: Telecom arm draws 87% revenue; rising debt costs signal caution The sharp listing-day rally, however, has already taken the stock 3.8–5.9% above their 12-month price targets, raising questions about how much of Jio's growth potential is already reflected in its valuation. Nomura, which initiated coverage on Wednesday with a target price of Rs 1,340, had projected an upside of nearly 20% from the issue price. The brokerage expects Jio to leverage its high data consumption per subscriber and low customer churn to drive ARPU growth. An anticipated industry-wide tariff hike in November–December 2026 could provide an immediate earnings trigger. Nomura also identified home broadband expansion, international licensing opportunities for Jio's proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology and declining capital expenditure as key growth drivers. Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL), which set a target price of Rs 1,350, expects Jio to consolidate its leadership in wireless services. It projects a 100-basis-point increase in the company's revenue market share between FY26 and FY29, alongside Jio accounting for 73% of incremental industry subscriber additions in home broadband during the period. The brokerage also sees significant opportunities beyond traditional connectivity services. “Scaling up its digital platforms, including cloud, enterprise communications, internet of things (IoT), and managed services, along with international tie-ups for its 5G/UBR technology, will offer the next leg of growth beyond the connectivity business,” MOFSL said. ALSO READJio IPO listing: Buy, Hold or Avoid? Top market experts weigh in Elara Capital, which assigned the highest target price among the three at Rs 1,367, is particularly bullish on Jio's emerging digital services business. The brokerage believes Jio is leveraging its affordable data offerings and extensive telecom network to build a large-scale digital products and services ecosystem catering to consumers and enterprises. Elara expects digital services revenue to double by FY30, expanding at twice the pace of the telecom business and emerging as the company's biggest growth driver. Meanwhile, Jio's telecom subscriber base is projected to grow at 3% annually between FY26 and FY29, supported by affordable tariffs, extensive network coverage and low churn.

docs.title: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta: Why the AI infrastructure deal is important
docs.text: Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms as the Facebook parent steps up its investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. AMD will also invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering, taking the combined investment from the two chipmakers to $4 billion. The investments come as Meta plans to raise up to $97.5 billion to fund its AI infrastructure expansion. This will be the largest fundraising effort in the Meta's history. Meta announced its fundraising plan on Monday, initially proposing to raise $35 billion through underwritten public equity offerings, followed by another $60 billion through an at-the-market programme. The company subsequently increased its overall fundraising target to $97.5 billion. The funds will support Meta's core business and emerging AI opportunities, including its family of apps, AI models and the infrastructure needed to develop and run them. ALSO READThe volatility of agentic chatter Nvidia and Meta make their AI partnership solid Nvidia said on Monday, October 26, that it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering and expand its partnership with the company on Muse, Meta's AI assistant and family of models. The companies will work together to improve the training and inference performance of Muse models. Training involves teaching an AI model to recognise patterns and generate responses. Nvidia said Meta's Muse models and agents use its computing infrastructure and have delivered strong benchmark performance and rising consumer downloads since their launch. Meta also intends to expand its deployment of Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems and Vera central processing units. The company will additionally use Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4 technology to improve network efficiency and support its growing AI workloads. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a press statement, “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf.” “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents,” Huang added. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said, “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We're excited to keep working with NVIDIA to deliver the best personal agents and frontier models for billions of people.” The companies are also considering further collaboration on Nvidia's OpenShell framework, which is designed to support the safe deployment of AI agents, and its Sentry technology for monitoring agent behaviour. ALSO READ‘Data centre in a container’: The multibillion-dollar opportunity and 2 stocks to watch Why Muse is important to Meta's AI plans Muse is central to Zuckerberg's ambition to bring more advanced, personalised AI capabilities to the billions of people who use Meta's services. According to Reuters, the assistant, known internally as Hatch, is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw. It can access applications covering email, calendars, payments, health, shopping and smart-home services, subject to user permissions that can be revoked. Unlike conventional chatbots that mainly respond to prompts, AI agents are designed to use tools and carry out tasks on behalf of users. Their ability to perform more complex tasks could make them an important part of Meta's Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp ecosystem. Developing these capabilities requires substantial computing power. Meta's expanded partnership with Nvidia is intended to improve model performance while reducing the cost of training and running AI systems. The focus on inference is particularly important as AI services attract more users. Every interaction with an AI assistant requires computing resources, making efficiency a key consideration as usage increases. AMD also invests as chipmakers expand their ties with Meta AMD announced a $1 billion investment in Meta's equity offering, adding a financial commitment to its existing technology partnership with the company. AMD said its Helios racks were already running at Meta, while its EPYC processors were powering Meta's Muse. The company is also working with Meta on infrastructure designed to operate at gigawatt scale. AMD CEO Lisa Su said, “Together, we are building and deploying infrastructure at gigawatt scale and shaping future generations of silicon, software and systems to enable Meta’s most ambitious superintelligence models and services.” Meta had previously said that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom had expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion in shares collectively. The disclosed investments from Nvidia and AMD account for $4 billion of that amount. Why the deal is important for the AI industry The investments show how the relationship between major technology companies and chipmakers is evolving. Nvidia and AMD are not only supplying the processors needed to build AI infrastructure but are also investing in companies that rely on their technology. Nvidia has expanded its investments across the AI industry. According to Dealroom data cited by CNBC, it participated in 121 investment rounds in 2026, compared with 13 in 2022. Its investments include OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel and xAI. AMD has also increased its investment activity, participating in 25 funding rounds in 2026, up from two in 2022. In July, the company said it would make an equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic.

docs.title: Diwali 2026 stock picks: Axis Securities names 9 Muhurat stocks for Samvat 2083
docs.text: Diwali is a time for new beginnings. For many investors, it also means opening a fresh page in the stock market. This year, though, the old page is hard to forget. Samvat 2082 left the Nifty 50 down 10.3%. So as Samvat 2083 begins, one question hangs in the air. Is this the moment to buy, or to wait? Axis Securities has picked nine stocks it wants investors to watch in Samvat 2083. Here is what it says, and why. The recommendations come after a volatile year for Indian equities, with earnings performance and valuations likely to influence returns over the next 12 months. 9 stocks Axis Securities is watching this Diwali The brokerage’s list includes DCB Bank, Nephrocare Healthcare Services, APL Apollo Tubes, Eternal, Elecon Engineering Company, Indian Hotels Company, Coforge, Ashok Leyland and Hindalco Industries. These picks reflect several themes identified by Axis Securities for the new Samvat year. DCB Bank represents the private banking theme, which the brokerage links to the credit growth cycle. Nephrocare Healthcare Services fits the diagnostics theme, with a focus on moving from testing towards early detection. APL Apollo Tubes reflects opportunities in building materials and capacity expansion, while Eternal represents the quick-commerce theme. Elecon Engineering Company and Hindalco Industries offer exposure to engineering and metals, respectively. Indian Hotels Company represents discretionary spending on travel and hospitality, while Ashok Leyland brings an automobile-focused idea to the list. Coforge fits the technology theme, which the brokerage connects with artificial intelligence-led transformation and a possible recovery in technology spending. ALSO READ15-fold dividend jump, 3.2% yield: A shipping PSU for your 2027 watchlist Why the market correction matters Samvat 2082 was difficult for Indian equities. According to the brokerage report, the Nifty 50 fell 10.3% up to October 23, 2026. The Nifty 500 declined 7.8%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 250 dropped 4.5% and 3.7%, respectively. Geopolitical tension, high crude oil prices, rising global bond yields, a stronger US dollar and foreign investor selling weighed on sentiment. Axis Securities describes the situation as “Correction Improves Entry Points”, while stressing that investors should focus on business performance and sensible valuations rather than buy indiscriminately. Stock price recovery linked to earnings performance The brokerage suggests investors pay close attention to results and management commentary over the coming months. At the time of the report, 16 Nifty 50 companies had announced their Q2 earning for FY26–27. Their year-on-year revenue, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), and profit after tax (PAT) grew 15%, 15% and 19%, respectively. However, performance remains uneven across companies and sectors. Axis Securities says “Delivery Will Matter More Than Promises” and advises investors to monitor demand, profit margins, order inflows and management guidance. Is the market more reasonably valued? The correction has also changed the market’s valuation picture. According to the report, the Nifty was trading at 16.4 times its one-year forward earnings, below its long-term average of 18.4 times. The brokerage also noted that India’s valuation premium over emerging markets has narrowed. ALSO READDalal Street Diwali sale: Kotak adds 5 midcaps with up to 37% upside — Full list Eight triggers that could change market sentiment Axis Securities identifies several developments that could influence equities in Samvat 2083. These include a decline in crude oil prices, easing geopolitical tension in West Asia, interest-rate developments, a recovery in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows and stronger corporate earnings. Progress on an India–United States trade agreement, continued government capital expenditure, resilient domestic investment and easing inflation could also support sentiment. The report noted that monthly systematic investment plan (SIP) contributions reached Rs 32,490 crore in September 2026. Brent crude, which rose to around US$114 per barrel on October 24 is another key factor to watch. A sustained decline towards US $85-90 per barrel could ease costs for several industries. What should investors watch now The brokerage’s outlook remains “Constructive, but Disciplined”. It expects market volatility to continue as global developments, oil prices, currency movements and company earnings shape investor sentiment. docs.title: Can silver hit $100 an ounce again?
docs.text: Silver prices in the futures market edged lower but held steady in the opening session of trade on Wednesday. On 28 October, silver opened at Rs 1,93,983 per kg on MCX. That was Rs 1,790 higher than Tuesday’s close of Rs 1,92,193 per kg. The 04 DEC 2026 contract was trading at Rs 1,95,170 per kg, down Rs 1,547, or 0.79%. Silver has crashed nearly 50% from its all-time high of Rs 3,84,632 per kg, hit on 29 January this year. With the festive season nearing, it remains to be seen if demand can push silver prices higher. Meanwhile, the most important near-term trigger for silver prices is today’s Federal Reserve decision. The benchmark interest rate is expected to remain at 3.75%-4.00%. If policymakers sound more hawkish than expected, higher real yields and a stronger dollar could push silver lower. On the other hand, any dovish stance hinting at possible monetary easing could bring back investment demand and support a recovery for silver. ALSO READGold nears $4,000: 7 global triggers driving prices that investors cannot ignore Why Is Silver Falling Harder Abroad Than in India? The price of silver in India depends on international prices, where the metal is traded in US dollars. Silver traded below $54 an ounce on Wednesday after rising for two straight sessions. Investors are cautiously awaiting the US Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy decision. The Fed is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged. Traders will, however, look for clues on a possible rate hike in December. The price crash of silver in the international market is more pronounced. From an all-time high of $121 hit on 29 January this year, the drop is nearly 55%. But it was not a one-way fall. From a 15 July low of $54, silver prices touched $70, a bounce of nearly 30% from the lows. Then came another slide, and silver now trades at the same level. In comparison, the fall in Indian markets is smaller. This is largely on account of the 9% import duty hike implemented in May this year and the depreciation of the rupee against the dollar. India vs international fall from peak MarketPeakCurrentFallIndia (MCX)Rs 3,84,632 per kgRs 1,95,359 per kgNearly 50%International$121 per ounceBelow $54 per ounceNearly 55% Source: Trading Economics The Fed and Oil Are the Biggest Worries So, what is pulling silver prices down? The biggest risk, possibly, remains the US Fed’s rate stance. US inflation remains much above the Fed’s target and could rise further, as oil prices stay elevated above $115. A resolution to the US-Iran war is not in sight either. Factors pressuring silver FactorData pointUS Fed rateExpected to stay at 3.75% to 4.00%, with a December hike possibleOil pricesAbove $115US dollar indexAbove 102 for many weeks10-year bond yieldAbove 5% Source: Trading Economics A Strong Dollar and 5% Yields Add to the Pressure The US dollar index is gaining strength and has stayed above 102 for many weeks now. This comes on the back of a “higher for longer” interest rate scenario, as the US Fed is expected to hike rates in December. Further, 10-year bond yields have again moved above 5%. Global inflation is pushing yields to multi-decade highs across the developed world. Higher yields continue to increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding precious metals like gold and silver. Historically, both gold and silver, the two precious metals, shine during periods of fear and economic uncertainty. Gold’s bull run began in late 2022, followed by the bull run in silver. The other factor linked to silver is gold’s performance, as gold plays a role in how silver moves. If sentiment on gold stays bullish, that should help sustain silver. When both metals rally, silver tends to do better than gold. Silver is more volatile than gold. It rises and falls more than gold does. A study by DSP Mutual Fund found that silver outperformed gold in only 10 out of 26 years. But when both precious metals rally, silver tends to outperform gold by a wide margin. This also means there are times when gold is the dominant driver of silver. At other times, silver is driven more by its own fundamentals. Can Silver Get Back to $100 an Ounce? Investors who entered the rally late could be sitting on losses. Only a major recovery could help them erase their losses. So, will silver cross Rs 3.5 lakh per kg in the Indian market, or move above $100 in the international market? For now, the headwinds look strong, and any major upmove may not be immediate. “The market may now be entering a period of consolidation with a slight upwards trajectory. Our views on gold are mildly supportive of silver going forward. We do not necessarily expect a rapid or robust near-term rally but look for more moderate gains in 2027. This should lend some support to silver and help put a floor on losses,” says James Steel, Chief Precious Metals Analyst at HSBC Securities (USA) Inc. “USD strength and high yields in and out of the US are both negative for silver, as are weaker industrial and jewelry demand and increased mine and recycling supply. For these reasons, and short of an eruption of tariff concerns, we do not see silver challenging $100 per ounce in the foreseeable future,” adds Steel. The broader silver market outlook remains influenced by the balance between industrial demand, mine production and structural supply constraints. Ultimately, the Fed’s commentary on inflation, employment and the future direction of borrowing costs will decide whether silver’s recovery can turn into sustained upward momentum. docs.title: Down 56.5%, trading at 23.5x earnings: An AI smallcap worth a fresh look
docs.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities for analytics companies. But a growing market does not automatically translate into higher profits. Companies still have to win clients, replace lost business and ensure that the money spent on new technology brings in enough revenue to justify the cost. Latent View Analytics is trying to do just that. The company helps businesses use data to make decisions and is investing in AI capabilities while deepening its relationship with Databricks, a data and AI platform. The opportunity is clear. Whether it can turn that opportunity into sustained growth without sacrificing margins is less certain. There are reasons to be optimistic. Latent View’s revenue grew 19.4% in US dollar terms in FY26, supported by growth in financial services and other non-technology businesses. Its Databricks-related business is also expanding, giving it another potential source of revenue as companies invest in data infrastructure and AI. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Latent View Analytics 1-Year Share Price Chart Source: Screener.in A large technology client has reduced its business with Latent View, leaving the company with revenue to replace even as it continues to invest in AI, Databricks and senior talent. These investments may support future growth, but they also raise costs in the present. The company now has to demonstrate that new business can make up for what it has lost. Investors are becoming less willing to overlook these challenges. At Rs 225.30 on 26 October 2026, the stock was down around 56.5% from its 52-week high of Rs 517.50. The key question is whether Latent View can turn the AI opportunity into profitable growth. The challenge of replacing lost business For a services company, losing a large client is not just a question of replacing revenue. It also leaves the company with employees and costs that were supported by that business. Finding another client takes time, while salaries and other expenses continue to be paid. ALSO READ4 Smallcap Stocks to Watch for Long-Term Growth Navigating the Tech Vertical Slump Latent View saw this problem play out in its technology vertical, which declined 9.5% sequentially in the March 2026 quarter. Vendor consolidation, project rationalisation and a large client’s decision to bring some work in-house contributed to the fall. The company expects the lost business to have an annualised revenue impact of around US$6.5 million to US$7 million in FY27. Source: Company Presentation Management hopes to recover part of this through new AI-led deals and an improvement in technology spending. But new business does not arrive on a timetable that neatly matches the loss of old business. Until replacement revenue comes in, the company must contend with a gap between the costs it carries and the revenue it generates. There is some support elsewhere in the business. Latent View’s non-technology segments grew around 41% in FY26, helped by demand from areas such as financial services. The question is whether this growth can continue at a pace that offsets weakness in technology. Diversification helps, but it becomes a real cushion only when it can absorb a setback in one of the larger businesses. The Growth-Margin Paradox: Why More AI Means Less Profit The case for Latent View rests partly on a simple proposition: as companies adopt AI, they will need help making their data usable, connecting systems and building applications that deliver business results. This creates work for analytics companies even when the underlying AI models are developed by someone else. Latent View has been investing in these capabilities. Its FY26 commentary indicated that advanced AI accounted for about 49% of revenue when customer-facing AI implementations and AI embedded in workflows were combined. The company’s Q1 FY27 presentation reported AI-led revenue at around 35%, using a narrower definition. These figures are not directly comparable, but they suggest that AI-related work is already a meaningful part of the business. The more difficult question is what this growth costs. Latent View has been investing in specialised employees, senior leadership and newer technology platforms. In the March 2026 quarter, its adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 24.1%, partly because of higher visa expenses and spending on AI and Databricks. In the June quarter, the margin declined further to 20.4%. This is the tension in the AI opportunity. A company cannot afford to stand still while its clients change how they use technology. But investing ahead of demand means carrying costs before the revenue fully arrives. If new projects scale up, today’s spending could support tomorrow’s growth. If they do not, the company could end up with higher costs without a corresponding improvement in revenue. AI demand, by itself, is therefore not enough to establish the strength of the investment case. Investors also need to see whether that demand translates into profitable business. Databricks could become a bigger contributor Latent View’s relationship with Databricks gives it another way to participate in the growth of AI. Companies preparing their data infrastructure for AI applications may need help with data engineering, platform integration and analytics. A services provider with the right skills and client relationships can benefit from this spending. Latent View generated US$17.5 million in Databricks-related revenue in FY26, an increase of around 46% over the previous year. Management had indicated an ambition to grow this business by around 60% in FY27. If that happens, Databricks could make a larger contribution to the company’s overall growth. docs.title: Jio Platforms: Motilal recommends long-term investment but Nomura prefers Bharti Airtel
docs.text: Jio Platforms’ Rs 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) closed for subscription on October 23, 2026, with the company fixing the issue price at Rs 1,119 per share and the listing on October 28, valuing the company at around Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Motilal Oswal Wealth Management sees long-term value citing Jio’s market leadership, earnings growth and opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI. Nomura, meanwhile prefers Bharti Airtel, citing its premium subscriber mix and stronger ability to benefit from tariff increases. Jio Platforms IPO closes, listing scheduled for October 28 Jio Platforms’ IPO carried a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share and comprised an entirely fresh issue of shares, with no offer for sale. At the upper end of the price band, the issue implied a market capitalisation of around Rs 10.3 lakh crore. The IPO proceeds were intended primarily for the prepayment or repayment of borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, Jio Platforms’ material subsidiary, with the balance allocated to general corporate purposes. Motilal Oswal’s report listed up to Rs 27,500 crore for repayment or prepayment of borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm. The subscription window has closed, so Motilal Oswal’s recommendation to subscribe applied to investors considering the IPO during its offer period. Those who missed the issue will have to assess the stock after listing, at the prevailing market price. That price may be above or below the IPO price of Rs 1,119. ALSO READDouble-digit profit growth, stocks down up to 43%: 4 names worth a fresh look Motilal Oswal recommends long-term investment Motilal Oswal Wealth Management’s report, titled Jio Platforms Limited, Subscribe for Listing Gains and Long Term, gave a positive view of the company’s market position, financial performance and growth opportunities. “Overall, we recommend investors to SUBSCRIBE for both listing gains and long term,” the brokerage said. The report added, “Jio offers a combination of market leadership, healthy earnings growth and future opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI.” Motilal Oswal’s investment case rested on Jio’s scale in digital connectivity, improving monetisation and operating leverage. The brokerage described Jio as India’s largest digital connectivity platform by subscriber base, carrying around 60% of the country’s wireless data traffic. It also pointed to the company’s nationwide 5G network, built on proprietary technology, and its growing fixed wireless broadband business under JioAirFiber. Jio revenue and profit growth betwee FY24-FY26 Motilal Oswal highlighted Jio’s consistent growth and profitability, with revenue and profit after tax growing at compound annual growth rates of around 16% and 18%, respectively, between FY24 and FY26. The brokerage noted that revenue and EBITDA grew around 11.8% and 15%, respectively, year on year in the June quarter. Motilal Oswal also pointed to cash generation as 5G capital expenditure moderated. EBITDA less cash capital expenditure increased to Rs 42,071.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,449.1 crore in FY24, according to the report. Jio Platform ARPU, tariff hike, broadband key monitorables Motilal Oswal identified improving monetisation as another strength. Jio’s average revenue per user (ARPU) increased from Rs 181.7 in FY24 to Rs 214 in FY26 and Rs 215.6 in the June 2026 quarter. The brokerage said higher data consumption, tariff hikes and fixed broadband expansion offered scope for further growth. Jio’s proprietary 5G technology, JioAirFiber business and enterprise and cloud offerings provided additional opportunities, although their contribution to earnings would need to grow over time. The report also identified risks. Connectivity remained the main earnings driver, and monetisation of newer digital services and AI offerings had yet to be demonstrated at scale. Motilal Oswal listed capital intensity, tariff and competition risks, spectrum and licensing requirements, promoter control, and technology and security as areas to monitor.
