docs.title: 2 ‘underdog’ stocks Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia just added to their portfolios
docs.text: Mukul Agrawal and Vijay Kedia portfolio: 2 new stocks in the September 2026 filings The September 2026 shareholding filings have thrown up two names few investors knew a quarter ago. Both are small. Both trade on NSE Emerge, the exchange's platform for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). And both now carry the name of a market veteran on their register. Mukul Agrawal, who runs Param Capital, has taken a position in a Hyderabad maker of metal powders and tungsten parts that end up in rockets. Vijay Kedia, known for his SMILE approach to small companies, shows up in a Gujarat maker of technical yarns that listed only in September. The more telling detail is not what they bought. It is the price each paid to get in. One word of caution before the numbers. SME stocks follow lighter disclosure rules, trade in fixed lots rather than single shares, and can be hard to exit when buyers dry up. Read every figure below with that in mind. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Innomet Advanced Materials: Mukul Agrawal's Rs 25 crore tungsten defence bet Incorporated in 1984, Innomet Advanced Materials moved from diamond tools into metal powders in 2004 and now runs two divisions. One makes copper, bronze and nickel powders for auto parts and welding. The other, called Innotung, makes tungsten heavy alloys, an extremely dense metal used in defence, aerospace and radiation shielding. On its June 2026 earnings call, filed with NSE, the management said the company is qualified to supply pre-fragments for Pinaka rockets. It counts HAL and BDL among its tungsten customers. It also said China's curbs on tungsten exports have pushed buyers to look at India as an alternative. That is the hook for defence stock watchers. As per the September 2026 shareholding filing, Mukul Agrawal holds 2,26,200 shares, or about 1.7% of the company, worth roughly Rs 6.2 cr at today's price. The bigger move came next. On 23rd October 2026, the company informed NSE that it had allotted 11,92,200 warrants to him at Rs 210 each, a commitment of about Rs 25 cr. Each warrant can be converted into one share. Here is the twist. On 18th August 2026, Innomet had issued 4.5 lakh shares to non-promoter investors and 5 lakh warrants to its promoters, all at Rs 131. Mukul Agrawal's warrants are priced 60% higher. That gap reflects timing more than generosity, because SEBI's pricing rules tie such issues to recent trading prices, and the stock ran hard in between. If every warrant is converted, his holding would rise to roughly 9.4% of the enlarged share base. ALSO READ7x earnings, a 59% fall: Vijay Kedia and Dolly Khanna’s latest smallcap bets Innomet financials: 34% sales CAGR, but the profit line tells another story Financial YearFY21FY22FY23FY24FY25FY265Y CAGRSales (Rs cr)12.3022.1823.2924.9032.5253.8134%EBITDA (Rs cr)1.121.695.734.365.055.6038%Net Profit (Rs cr)0.200.553.222.521.871.57NM Source: Screener.in EBITDA here refers to operating profit before other income. NM: not meaningful, as the FY21 base is near zero. Sales have more than quadrupled in five years, and FY26 revenue alone jumped 66%. Profit is a different matter. Its five-year growth rate only looks dazzling because it starts from Rs 0.20 cr. Over three years, net profit has in fact shrunk by about 21% a year, from Rs 3.22 cr in FY23 to Rs 1.57 cr in FY26. Other income of Rs 0.32 cr also made up about 13% of FY26 pre-tax profit. The second half of FY26 was the weak spot. Sales rose to Rs 30.33 cr, yet the operating margin fell to 4.5% and the company posted a small loss of Rs 0.44 cr. The management blamed a sudden spike in tungsten and copper prices. It also wrote off Rs 1.92 cr of development costs the auditor could not validate, and reversed Rs 2.96 cr of revenue booked for a technology deal that fell through. Order book, Israel exports and the Swastik Tungsten buy The bull case rests on what comes next. Orders worth Rs 35.99 cr were booked in the first two months of FY27, the management said. That is more than half of last year's revenue, and about 77% of it is tungsten heavy alloys. A single export order from Israel's Scope Metals was pegged at about Rs 15 cr. In February 2026, Innomet also bought 57.5% of Swastik Tungsten through the NCLT route for around Rs 1.5 cr, to secure raw material. On 13th October, it disclosed fresh orders from Federal-Mogul Goetze and a Japanese buyer. Innomet share price and PE ratio: Priced at 228x earnings Innomet came to market in September 2024 at Rs 100 a share and listed at Rs 190. The share price of Innomet then slid to a 52-week low of Rs 63.2. A sharp rally took it to Rs 276 as of closing on 27th October 2026, more than four times that low. Shareholders have grown from 799 in September 2024 to 1,255. As for valuation, the stock trades at a PE of about 228x against a current industry median of about 20x. A 10-year median PE does not exist yet, as the stock has been listed for just over two years. At over eight times book value, with return on equity of 3.7% and return on capital of 5.7%, the price is a bet on the order book, not the past. Promoter holding slipped to 55.02% in September 2026 from 56.72% in March, largely because new shares went to other investors. More dilution lies ahead as warrants convert. ALSO READMukul Agrawal’s latest moves: A Rs 189 cr mining bet and 4 newly listed SME stocks #2 Ashutosh Fibre: Vijay Kedia's pre-IPO stake in a technical textile stock Incorporated in 1985, Ashutosh Fibre makes technical and synthetic yarns at a single plant in Petlad, Gujarat. These are not yarns for shirts. They go into filters, flame-retardant workwear, PPE kits, car seat fabric and carpets. Its IPO document, filed with NSE, shows exports made up about 39% of FY26 revenue, with China its largest export market. Kedia did not buy this one on the open market. He was already a shareholder before the IPO, with 6.57%

docs.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On takes on spatial awareness with AI: Should you buy it?
docs.text: After leaving us impressed with the Galaxy Buds 4 range earlier this year, Samsung has now ventured into the open-ear clip-in earbuds category. The Galaxy Buds On is the company's first open-ear clip-on wireless earbuds similar to the many options already available from Sony, Nothing and various other audio brands, but Samsung’s idea is to bring hands-free Google Gemini Live interactions into everyday commuting and fitness routines. At the moment, the Galaxy Buds On have been revealed in South Korea only and Samsung is expected to bring it to our shores in the coming months. Unlike the Galaxy Buds 4 and Apple AirPods 5, the new earbuds bypass traditional in-ear silicone seals entirely, relying instead on a flexible shape-memory alloy band that clips around the outer ear while leaving the ear canal completely unblocked. Galaxy Buds On features at a glance Unlike traditional in-ear Galaxy Buds, the Galaxy Buds On feature an outer-ear clip-on design constructed with a flexible shape-memory alloy band. Sitting outside the ear canal, they promise all-day wearability without the pressure build-up common to sealed tips. And then there’s the audio performance, which makes a lot of promises. Samsung Galaxy Buds On ALSO READWho should choose Apple’s new 14-inch MacBook Pro? TwinBoost speaker drivers: Open-ear designs historically suffer from weak bass response. Samsung addresses this with TwinBoost speakers engineered specifically to enhance low-frequency output, delivering punchy bass lines without requiring an ear-canal seal. Audio leakage reduction : Utilising phase-cancellation acoustic tuning, the earbuds prevent sound spill, ensuring private calls and personal playlists remain unheard by nearby commuters. Qualcomm Snapdragon S7 Gen 1 architecture: Powered by the S7 Gen 1 Sound Platform with an integrated Class-D amplifier, the buds optimise high-fidelity sound output while maintaining up to 9.5 hours of continuous playback on a single charge. Gemini Live makes the difference While most open-ear earbuds function primarily as passive audio conduits, the Galaxy Buds On act as an active ambient engine driven by Google’s Gemini Live. Hands-free Gemini Live interactions: Simply saying "Hey Google, let's talk Live" initiates a continuous conversational stream with Gemini AI directly through the headset. Users can access real-time information, navigate routes, or manage tasks mid-workout without touching a phone or tapping an earbud. Dynamic auto-volume and adaptive ambient balance: Integrated micro-mics analyse surrounding noise floor shifts in real time, balancing ambient clarity with media levels automatically. Samsung says that passing a noisy construction site elevates speech clarity, while stepping into a quiet room normalises volume to prevent acoustic shock. Intelligent Clear Call system: Combining a 3-microphone array, a bone-conduction Voice Pickup Unit (VPU), and machine-learning noise-suppression algorithms, the Buds On isolate vocal acoustics even against severe wind noise. Natural Head Gesture control: Built-in motion sensors allow users to answer or decline incoming calls, dismiss alarms, and interact with incoming notification readouts using intuitive head nods or shakes. Instant Voice Memo recording: A touch-and-hold shortcut activates high-fidelity voice note recording, which is indexed and transcribed for voice search through Samsung Bixby. Galaxy Buds On vs. AirPods Pro 3: A quick comparo Apple's flagship AirPods Pro 3 focus heavily on health-centric monitoring, whereas the Galaxy Buds On target continuous environmental integration. FeatureSamsung Galaxy Buds OnApple AirPods Pro 3Form Factor & FitOpen-Ear Clip-On (Shape-Memory Alloy)In-Ear Sealed (Silicone Tips + Active Pressure Relief)Acoustic StrategyOpen-Air Ambient Blend + Sound Leakage ReductionActive Noise Cancellation (ANC) + Adaptive AudioAI IntegrationGoogle Gemini Live (Conversational Real-time AI)Siri + Apple Intelligence Contextual AssistancePrimary FocusEnvironmental Awareness & Voice WorkflowsBiometric Health Tracking & Spatial AudioHealth & Fitness SensorsBasic Activity & Gesture Motion TrackingPhotoplethysmography (PPG) Heart Rate & Calorie SensorsHands-Free ControlNatural Head Gestures (Nod / Shake) + Live VoiceStem Pinch / Capacitive Touch + Siri Voice TriggersBattery Life (Single Charge)Up to 9.5 HoursUp to 8 Hours (ANC on) / 6.5 Hours (Workout + Heart Rate) Determining which earbud is "smarter" depends entirely on how intelligence is defined within a personal workflow. ALSO READCracking under pressure: Inside Apple’s iPhone Duo screen damage controversy The AirPods Pro 3 are the health specialists. For users who view ear-worn wearables as biometric instruments, Apple wins. By tracking optical heart rate metrics continuously during workouts via PPG sensors, the AirPods Pro 3 function as a dedicated health sensor node directly integrated into Apple Fitness. The Galaxy Buds On are the ambient and conversational experts. By combining an open-ear shape with Gemini Live, the Galaxy Buds On create a non-intrusive computing layer. You remain fully present in your surroundings while engaging in fluid, natural conversation with an AI assistant.

docs.title: Gold Prices Falling: 3 Gold ETFs With the Lowest Cost of Tracking Gold
docs.text: Gold has had a rough autumn. Gold's LBMA PM benchmark price reached US$5,120 an ounce on 24 February, and by 23 October spot gold was near US$ 4,016, roughly 21% lower. This week alone it lost about 3.5%, its steepest weekly drop in more than four months, as rising oil prices pushed traders to expect that US interest rates will stay higher for longer. In India, gold ETFs gave back about 6.8% in a month and about 3.3% in a week, yet they are still up about 13% over one year and about 31% per annum over three years. For anyone looking at gold ETFs after a fall like this, the metal is only half the question. Every gold ETF in India tracks the same domestic price of gold, so the real difference between funds is how closely and how cheaply they follow it. Among the 11 ETFs that have both a 3-year and a 5-year record, three stand out on returns and tracking error together. Let’s look at each in detail. #1 UTI Gold ETF First on the list is UTI Gold ETF. UTI is the only fund that sits in the top three on all three measures. It has the highest 3-year return (31.72%), the second-highest 5-year return (23.25%) and a tracking error of 0.29%, level with Quantum for the lowest of the 11. ALSO READThis Lesser-Known Mid Cap Fund Delivered 22.7% CAGR in 5 Years Its tracking difference, the gap between the fund and gold itself, is only about 1.0% a year over one, three and five years, which is the most consistent of any fund. LIC MF Gold ETF has the highest 5-year return of the 11 (23.47%) and the second-highest 3-year return (31.65%). It also has the smallest tracking difference over five years, at -0.78%, and the second-lowest expense ratio, at 0.45%. Its weak spot is tracking error. At 0.47% it ranks only joint ninth, which means its day-to-day path wanders more than UTI's even though its long-run result is excellent. docs.title: Aavas Financiers Q2 net profit rises 10.7%, but can low rains hurt the portfolio?
docs.text: Aavas Financiers reported stronger disbursements in the September quarter, supported by growth in its housing and non-housing loan businesses. However, pressure on lending spreads and a modest rise in overdue loans kept attention on the quality and profitability of its growth. Jefferies, Equirus Securities and InCred Capital remained positive on the company, although their views differed on the earnings outlook and valuation. Aavas Financiers Q2FY27 performance Aavas’ assets under management (AUM) rose 16.1% year on year to Rs 24,801 crore in Q2FY27. Disbursements increased 21.2% year on year to Rs 1,891 crore. The non-housing loan book grew 28.6%, compared with 10.1% growth in housing loans. Net interest income grew 12.7% year on year, while profit after tax rose 10.7%. Equirus noted that “Spread contraction drove an NII miss, while contained opex and lower provisions kept PPoP and PAT in line.” Gross stage 3 assets remained stable at 1.1%, while net stage 3 assets stood at 0.7%. Loans overdue by more than 30 days edged up to 3.81%. Jefferies maintains 'Buy' rating on Aavas Financiers Jefferies maintained its 'Buy' rating on Aavas Financiers. Jefferies’ assessment focused on asset quality and profitability. Gross stage 3 assets remained stable quarter on quarter, while overdue loans increased marginally. Pressure on lending margins remains important to the company’s earnings outlook. The report also discussed management’s expectation that the operating expense-to-assets ratio “should fall below 3% in the medium term.” Improving operating efficiency could support profitability as the loan book expands. ALSO READL&T to BEL, HAL: 12 defence stocks in focus after DAC clears Rs 2.12 lk cr procurement Equirus retains 'Long' rating on Aavas Financiers Equirus Securities retained its 'Long' rating and a September 2027 target price of Rs 1,795, implying 57.5% upside from the reference price. The brokerage forecast an 18% compound annual growth rate in AUM between FY26 and FY29, while trimming its margin estimates for FY27 and FY28. Equirus said there was “no impact of lower rains/drought on the portfolio quality and business momentum.” It also noted that management had retained its growth and credit-cost guidance. Aavas kept its FY27 AUM growth guidance at 16-17% and credit-cost guidance below 25 basis points. Equirus also noted that management expected spreads to remain above 5%, with employee productivity and operating cost control important to its longer-term plans. InCred Capital retains 'Add' rating but cuts target price InCred Capital retained its 'Add' rating but reduced its target price to Rs 1,550 from Rs 1,700, implying 36% upside from the reference price. The brokerage pointed to improving operating efficiency and loan growth, while noting that margins and asset quality remained key concerns. It wrote, “We appreciate the rising branch productivity to 1.25 files/month per officer vs 1.1 QoQ.” It also said, “Improving productivity and growth support outlook, although spread and asset quality remain key watchpoints.” InCred noted that disbursements rose 17% quarter on quarter and 21% year on year. It said Aavas had reiterated its guidance for around 20% year-on-year disbursement growth, with AUM growth of about 16-17% in FY27. Aavas Financiers outlook hinges on margins and productivity Aavas is expanding its loan book while keeping stage 3 asset ratios broadly stable, but margin pressure remains a key concern. Equirus expects sustained AUM growth, InCred sees scope for better productivity, and Jefferies’ view remains positive, although its latest target price could not be verified from the available report details. The company’s ability to convert stronger disbursements into sustained earnings growth will depend on managing funding costs, improving employee productivity and maintaining asset quality. docs.text: Defence stocks could draw attention after the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) approved capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 2.12 lakh crore for the Army, Navy and Air Force. Goldman Sachs identified potential beneficiaries across India’s defence manufacturing sector, including Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL), Bharat Electronics (BEL), Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and BEML. The proposals cover helicopters, combat vehicles, artillery systems, air defence equipment, drones, surveillance platforms and naval systems. Goldman Sachs noted that the DAC expects 82% of procurement to come from Indian industry, potentially supporting domestic manufacturers and subsystem suppliers. The Air Force proposals also include helicopters, air defence systems, weapons and mobile X-band Doppler weather radar systems. Goldman Sachs said Astra Microwave and Data Patterns could benefit from the weather radar procurement. Land systems & artillery: How BEML and L&T stand to gain The Army’s approved proposals include high-mobility vehicles, self-propelled tracked gun systems, gunshot response systems, light multi-role helicopters, very short-range air defence systems, counter-drone systems, surveillance unmanned aerial vehicles and long-range kamikaze drone systems. The self-propelled tracked gun system could create opportunities linked to the K9 Vajra-T howitzer, manufactured by Larsen & Toubro in partnership with Hanwha Aerospace. Goldman Sachs noted that the Army ordered 100 units in May 2017 for Rs 4,500 crore and awarded a further contract worth Rs 7,630 crore in 2024 for another 100 units. Counter-drone warfare: Niche tech players target VSHORAD orders The Army’s proposals also cover very short-range air defence systems and platform-based counter-unmanned aerial systems. These systems are intended to address aerial threats and improve the survivability of tanks on the battlefield. Goldman Sachs said Adani Defence & Aerospace and Apollo Micro Systems were likely to benefit from the very short-range air defence system procurement. For counter-drone systems, it identified Zen Technologies, Adani Aerospace & Defence and Solar Industries as potential beneficiaries, while noting that the configuration was not yet clear. The approved surveillance and drone systems are intended to improve the Army’s surveillance and targeting capabilities. The brokerage said that “a number of companies in the India drone ecosystem are likely to be benefit from this procurement.” BEL could gain from naval countermeasure systems For the Navy, the DAC approved the procurement of an Active Offboard Decoy System (AODS) and other major naval platforms. BEL already manufactures the Maareech Advanced Torpedo Decoy System and is the nodal production agency for integrating the electronics, launcher frameworks and command software for the newly approved surface AODS. docs.title: Jio listing strikes an emotional chord with Ambanis
docs.text: As Jio Platforms made its stock market debut on Wednesday, Mukesh Ambani found himself at the centre of a moment that went beyond the company's market milestone. As his children spoke of their father’s vision and the legacy of their grandfather, Dhirubhai Ambani, the Reliance Industries Chairman was visibly emotional, his eyes welling up at several points during the ceremony. For a family that has built one of the country's largest business empires across generations, the listing was as much a moment of reflection as a celebration of what lay ahead. ALSO READJio Platforms surges 21% on debut: Is a 15% tariff hike next? What Motilal Oswal forecasts The occasion brought together three generations of the Ambani family, with matriarch Kokilaben Ambani, Mukesh and Nita Ambani, and their children, Akash, with wife Shloka, Isha, with husband Anand Piramal, and Anant in attendance. The ceremony began with the national anthem and a traditional lamp-lighting, but as the speeches unfolded, the focus shifted from the company’s entry into the stock market to the people and ambitions behind it. Anant Ambani set the tone by describing the listing bell as a temple bell and business as puja. He traced Jio’s origins to Dhirubhai Ambani’s belief that ordinary Indians could aspire to extraordinary things. His grandfather had laid the foundation for that ambition, he said, while his father had taken it forward by envisioning a digitally connected India. The listing, in that sense, was another milestone in a journey that began long before Jio became a household name. Isha Ambani’s tribute brought the family’s history into sharper focus. She recalled how her father, at the age of 20, had worked on Reliance’s first public offering in 1977, when Dhirubhai took the company to ordinary investors rather than limiting ownership to the wealthy. Nearly five decades later, she said, that trust had come full circle. As she thanked her father, telling him, “We are here today because of you,” the audience applauded, while Mukesh Ambani’s emotional response lent the moment a personal poignancy. Akash Ambani spoke of learning at his father’s feet and of the responsibility that now rested on the three siblings. They were taking the baton from Mukesh, he said, and would work to prove themselves worthy of it. If Dhirubhai had laid the foundation and Mukesh had carried the vision into the digital age, the next generation would have to take it further. ALSO READMissed Jio IPO allotment? Analysts reveal entry levels for the telecom stock after listing The family came together to ring the opening bell, bringing the ceremony to its formal climax. Yet some of the day's more intimate moments unfolded away from the dais. The Ambani grandchildren moved about and played as the proceedings continued, briefly lending the carefully choreographed event the feel of a family gathering. At one point, a child walked up to the dais while Isha was speaking. The celebrations extended to Reliance Corporate Park in Ghansoli, where colourful streamers and illuminated trees marked the occasion. The campus, home to an estimated 12,000-15,000 employees, hosted food stalls and activity kiosks, turning the day into a gathering for the workforce as well.

docs.title: Here's why Motilal Oswal sees 34% upside in Vedanta Aluminium despite cutting target price
docs.text:
Published On Oct 29, 2026 | 06:48 IST 
 Last Updated On Oct 29, 2026 | 08:18 IST 
 AI Summary
 Vedanta Aluminium is targeting sharp production cost reductions through backward integration and expanding captive alumina supplies, even as near-term expenses rise due to planned power plant shutdowns. Analysts expect earnings to surge on higher output and robust domestic demand. Can upcoming regional capacity expansions in West Asia threaten global metal prices?
 Remove Ad 
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source 
 Shares of Vedanta Aluminium will be in focus on Thursday, October 29, after CLSA maintained its Outperform rating on the stock with a target price of ₹525, implying an upside of around 46% from Wednesday’s close of ₹359, while Motilal Oswal Financial Services retained its Buy rating but cut its target price to ₹480 from ₹500, indicating an upside of around 34%.
CLSA said Vedanta Aluminium’s Q2FY27 results were slightly ahead of expectations on lower costs. The firm expects the company to exit FY27 with an annualised earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) run rate of $5 billion at spot aluminium prices, supported by smelter ramp-ups and cost-saving projects.
Motilal Oswal, meanwhile, expects EBITDA to grow at a compound annual growth rate of around 22% between FY26 and FY28.
Vedanta Aluminium reported revenue of ₹22,324 crore in the September quarter , up 4.4% year-on-year (YoY), while net profit declined 6% to ₹6,187 crore. EBITDA fell 1.8% to ₹10,113 crore, and the EBITDA margin contracted to 45.3% from 48.1% a year earlier. 
 CLSA said investors would focus on capital allocation and the next phase of expansion, including a proposed 3-million-tonne aluminium smelter targeted for the end of FY28.
The global investment firm said the current share price reflects an aluminium price assumption of $2,650 per tonne, compared with spot prices of around $3,100 per tonne, and a target valuation multiple of five times, against six times in its base case. At four times estimated FY28 attributable enterprise value to EBITDA, CLSA sees a free cash flow yield of 19%. 
 Motilal Oswal said the September quarter was supported by higher volumes and favourable foreign exchange movements, partly offset by a sequential decline in London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium prices.
The firm said management expects hot metal cost of production to decline to around $1,550 per tonne after key integration initiatives are completed. This would be $150-$175 per tonne below first-half FY27 levels. The company expects savings of around $100-$125 per tonne by the end of FY27, with the remaining savings likely over the following one to two quarters.
Costs are expected to rise around 4% sequentially in the December quarter due to planned power plant shutdowns and higher carbon costs, before moderating in the March quarter. Overall costs in the second half of FY27 are expected to remain broadly in line with, or slightly below, first-half levels.
Motilal Oswal’s note put blended aluminium cost of production at $1,722 per tonne in Q2FY27, down 6% year-on-year but up from $1,698 per tonne in the June quarter. Alumina cost of production stood at $378 per tonne, broadly flat year-on-year and sequentially. 
 Aluminium output reached a quarterly record of 649 kilotonnes, up 5% year-on-year, while alumina production rose 37% to a record 895 kilotonnes.
Motilal Oswal said Vedanta Aluminium aims to increase the share of value-added products to more than 90%, supported by higher foundry alloy and billet production and greater domestic sales.
The company is progressively ramping up the third potline at Bharat Aluminium Company, targeting a full-capacity run rate of around 435 kilotonnes per annum by March 2027. Management expects alumina production to rise around 10% in the third and fourth quarters of FY27, reaching rated capacity by the end of the financial year.
The company also expects its captive alumina mix to increase to around 85% by the end of FY27, supported by higher refinery output, expanded supplies from Odisha Mining Corporation and the start of production at the Sijimali bauxite mine. The mine could generate savings of around $25 per tonne compared with imported bauxite, according to Motilal Oswal. 
 Motilal Oswal said management sees Indian aluminium demand growing around 40% between calendar years 2025 and 2030, supported by applications in power, transportation and lightweighting.
However, the firm cautioned that additional supply from West Asia and Indonesia could put pressure on aluminium prices if regional operations normalise. 
 According to Bloomberg's analyst consensus data, of 14 analysts covering Vedanta Aluminium, 13 have given it a Buy rating, and one has a Sell rating, with no Hold ratings. The 12-month consensus target price stood at ₹512.92, compared with the last price, implying a potential upside of around 43%.
Shares of Vedanta Aluminium closed 1.4% higher at ₹359 ahead of the earnings announcement on Wednesday. The stock has declined about 28% so far in 2026.

 Motilal Oswal's research report on Jio Platforms
